docs.text: Driver SE05X Driver ¶ A C++20 driver and hardware root-of-trust facade for the NXP EdgeLock SE050, SE051 and SE052 secure elements: T=1 over I2C, SCP03, the IoT applet, typed objects and policies, attestation and guarded irreversible operations, on any MCU. Choose your job The first 15 minutes API guide Source on GitHub The SE05x is a family of secure elements (SE050, SE051, SE052) that hold keys and credentials isolated from the host, sign, agree keys and attest with them inside the chip, and talk to the host over I2C with T=1 framing and an encrypted SCP03 channel (SE050 1 Introduction, p. 1). The three chips differ in package, applet, memory and certification: Where to use it helps you choose and draws the SE052's HVQFN20 package; the figures below show the HX2QFN20 of the SE050 and SE051. SE05x Figure description and sources The SE05x in the middle, drawn as its HX2QFN20 package. On the left the MCU that runs the driver, joined to it by I2C, T=1. To the right, what the chip drives, in the order the power flows. The tiles at the bottom are the headline numbers, each with the datasheet section and page it comes from. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . What it does ¶ What the SE05x does Figure description and sources Each card is one function of the SE05x: an icon, its name and what it does for the application. The filled pill says how this driver covers it (legend below); the outlined pills are the chip registers behind it. The coverage table in the README gives the driver calls and the datasheet section of each card. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . Where it is used ¶ Secure connection to public and private clouds and edge platforms Device-to-device authentication Protection of data such as sensor data (SE050 1 Introduction, p. 1) Wi-Fi credential protection: a device key for WPA-EAP-TLS (AN12661 2 Wi-Fi credential protection, p. 4) Secure commissioning, key storage and credential provisioning Ecosystem protection Smart industry, smart home, smart cities and smart supply chains (SE050 1.2 SE050 target applications, p. 2) Healthcare (SE052) (SE052 1.2 Applications, p. 1) Uses named by the datasheet (SE050 1.1 SE050 use cases, p. 1). Inside the chip ¶ Inside the SE05x Figure description and sources The SE05x's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . The block diagram is drawn from the functional description of the SE050 data sheet (sections 3 to 5), which has no block diagram of its own. It and the pinout and wiring figures below show the SE050 and SE051 in HX2QFN20, though their titles name the family. The SE052 has no ENA pin (SE052 Table 2, p. 4), so the power-switch block does not apply to it; SE052 draws its own pins and wiring. Pins and wiring ¶ SE05x pinout, HX2QFN20 Figure description and sources The SE05x seen from the top, in its HX2QFN20 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . Wiring: Recommended application (SE050, SE051) Figure description and sources The MCU on the left, the SE05x in the middle. Each wire to the chip is coloured by the chip pin's electrical type and carries the net name and the chip pin number above it and, under it, the driver hooks that use it (and any part on the net). The boxes underneath list the supplies, the support parts and the pins this circuit leaves unconnected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . Each wire to the chip is coloured by the chip pin's electrical type and carries the net name and the chip pin number above it and, under it, the driver hooks that use it (and any part on the net). The boxes underneath list the supplies, the support parts and the pins this circuit leaves unconnected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). SE05x: T=1 R-block (acknowledgement) Figure description and sources One T=1 R-block (acknowledgement) of the SE05x, 40 bits in a row from the most significant (left, sent first) to the least significant (right). Each row is one kind of frame; each coloured box a field, with its first and last bit number under it. The table at the bottom names each bit of the PCB field. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . Secure element SE050, SE051, SE052 NXP EdgeLock Function Key storage and use that never leaves the chip (SE050 1 Introduction, p. 1): sign and ECDH (AN12543 4.10, p. 101), attestation (AN12543 3.2.7.2, p. 19), counters (AN12543 3.2.1.7, p. 7), secure storage (AN12543 4.7.1.4, p. 84) Interface I2C target at 7-bit address 0x48 (SE050 4.1, Figure 3, p. 8; SE052 Table 12, p. 18), T=1 framing in two flavours (UM11225 Tables 1, 3 and 4, p. 5; GPC_SPE_172 I2C physical layer, p. 23), GlobalPlatform SCP03 and ECKey sessions (AN12543 3.5, p. 27) Packages HX2QFN20 (SE050, SE051; SE050 8 Package, p. 12), HVQFN20 (SE052; SE052 6 Package, p. 5) Control ENA on the SE050 and SE051 (SE050 5.2 Deep Power-down mode, p. 10), RST_N on the SE052 (SE052 Table 2, p. 4) Supply VIN 1.62 V to 3.6 V on the SE050 and SE051 (SE050 Table 9, p. 13); on the SE052 VIN 1.65 V to 3.6 V and VDD 1.62 V to 5.5 V (SE052 Table 13, p. 18) Every pin, the reference circuits, the bus settings, the timing and the power: Hardware . Quick start ¶ Wire the chip as above, write the port for your MCU ( Porting ), then: using BoardPorts = se05x :: Ports < MyBus , MyClock , se05x :: ReferenceCrypto > ; se05x :: Error RandomBytes ( MyBus & bus , MyClock & clock , se05x :: ReferenceCrypto & crypto , se05x :: MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { const BoardPorts ports ( bus , clock , crypto ); se05x :: Device < BoardPorts > device ( ports , se05x :: Config {}); if ( const auto opened = device . Open (); ! opened . ok ()) { return opened . error ; // for example DeviceIdMismatch: nothing answered like an SE05x } const auto random = device . GetRandom ( out ); static_cast < void > ( device . Close ()); return random . error ; } Every step, with the port and what to check when it does not work: Quickstart . Driver coverage ¶ Capability What the chip does Driver API Registers Status Datasheet Key generation Generates EC key pairs inside the chip under a policy; the private key never leaves it (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 4.7.1.1, p. 58)) Provision , GenerateEcKey , Execute WriteECKey ( WriteEcKey ), WriteSymmKey Supported AN12543 4.7.1.1 WriteECKey, p. 80 Signatures and key agreement ECDSA signatures and verification and ECDH shared secrets with keys held in the chip Sign , TlsSign , VerifySignature , Agree , EcdsaSign , EcdsaVerify ECDSASign ( EcdsaSign ), ECDSAVerify ( EcdsaVerify ), ECDHGenerateSharedSecret ( EcdhGenerateSharedSecret ) Supported AN12543 4.10 Crypto operations EC, p. 101 Attestation Proves a key or a value comes from this chip: a signed, fresh read with the chip's unique ID (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 3.2.7.2, p. 13)) Attest , ReadAttested ReadObject with attestation ( ReadObjectAttested ) Supported AN12543 3.2.7.2 Reading with attestation, p. 19 Secure storage Binary objects for secrets such as a Wi-Fi passphrase or a token, read only as their policy allows (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 4.7.1.4, p. 61)) Store , Load , WriteBinary , ReadObject WriteBinary , ReadObject Supported AN12543 4.7.1.4 WriteBinary, p. 84 Certificates and CSR Stores and reads certificates, builds a certificate request for a chip key and checks a chain (requests and chains in the optional PKI layer) StoreCertificate , LoadCertificate , BuildCsr , VerifyChain WriteBinary , ReadObject Supported AN12543 4.7.1.4 WriteBinary, p. 84 Monotonic counters Counters that only count up, for an anti-rollback floor on the firmware version (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 3.2.1.7, p. 8)) CreateCounter , RaiseCounterTo , CheckFloor , IncrementCounter WriteCounter Supported AN12543 3.2.1.7 Counter, p. 7 Secure channels Platform SCP03 encrypts the bus; AESKey, ECKey and UserID sessions authenticate the caller (ECKey sessions behind a build flag) Open , BeginAesKeySession , BeginEcKeySession , BeginUserIdSession , EndSession CreateSession , SCPInitializeUpdate ( ScpInitializeUpdate ), VerifySessionUserID ( VerifySessionUserId ) Supported AN12543 3.5 Secure Channel Protocols, p. 27 Lifecycle and locks Transport lock, a platform SCP03 requirement and factory reset: one-way changes to the chip (compiled out by default; each needs a plan and a typed confirmation) ExecuteIrreversible , Operations SetLockState , SetPlatformSCPRequest ( SetPlatformScpRequest ), DeleteAll Guarded AN12543 3.8 Lifecycle management, p. 42 Contactless and ISO 7816 The ISO 14443 antenna and ISO 7816 interfaces; the host cannot reach them over I2C - - Not covered SE050 4.2 ISO7816 and ISO14443 interface, p. 9 Supported : the driver covers it and a host test checks it; Guarded : covered, behind an explicit acknowledgement because a wrong value can do harm; Not covered : the chip has it and the driver leaves it alone. From docs/hardware.yml ; kokeb-docs hardware --check confirms that every API name is in inc/se05x_hrot.hpp , inc/se05x_device.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_csr.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_verify.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_device.hpp , inc/se05x_irreversible.hpp and every register (the header constant in brackets, where the header spells it otherwise) in inc/se05x_commands.hpp . The driver has no platform code. You give it small port classes (a bus and a clock, optionally reset and a hardware crypto engine); it does the framing, the secure channel, the checks and the recovery. What it does for you ¶ Provision Keys generated inside the chip, under a strict policy, in one call. Attest Prove a key or a value came from this chip; fresh, verified, typed. Sign and verify ECDSA, and EdDSA except on the SE052F in FIPS mode ( variants ), with keys that never leave the chip. ECDH Key agreement with the secret kept on the chip. Key import Wrapped import under a key-encryption key; no plain key on the host. Secure channels Platform SCP03, AESKey and ECKey sessions; no half-open channel. Secure storage Binary objects whose policy decides who reads them. Certificates Read the provisioned certificates, store your own. Counters Monotonic counters and anti-rollback floors. Lifecycle and lock Transport lock, SCP requirement, factory reset; irreversible steps guarded. Security model What the chip protects, what it does not, and the trust boundaries. Choose a variant SE050, SE051 or SE052, which applet and which authentication. What you get ¶ Layers with one job each. Link, APDU, secure channel, capability gate, objects, device, facade. See Architecture . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error and the chip's status word. See the API guide . A gate before the bus. A command the chip lacks never reaches it. See Contract . No foot-guns. Irreversible operations are separate types behind named confirmations, compiled out by default. See Safety rules . Honest about doubt. Every open question has a knob. See Ambiguities . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. See Contract . Tested without hardware. The tests run the driver against an independent model of the chip. See Testing and CI . Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 4.7.1.1, p. 58)) Provision , GenerateEcKey , Execute WriteECKey ( WriteEcKey ), WriteSymmKey Supported AN12543 4.7.1.1 WriteECKey, p. 80 Signatures and key agreement ECDSA signatures and verification and ECDH shared secrets with keys held in the chip Sign , TlsSign , VerifySignature , Agree , EcdsaSign , EcdsaVerify ECDSASign ( EcdsaSign ), ECDSAVerify ( EcdsaVerify ), ECDHGenerateSharedSecret ( EcdhGenerateSharedSecret ) Supported AN12543 4.10 Crypto operations EC, p. 101 Attestation Proves a key or a value comes from this chip: a signed, fresh read with the chip's unique ID (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 3.2.7.2, p. 13)) Attest , ReadAttested ReadObject with attestation ( ReadObjectAttested ) Supported AN12543 3.2.7.2 Reading with attestation, p. 19 Secure storage Binary objects for secrets such as a Wi-Fi passphrase or a token, read only as their policy allows (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 4.7.1.4, p. 61)) Store , Load , WriteBinary , ReadObject WriteBinary , ReadObject Supported AN12543 4.7.1.4 WriteBinary, p. 84 Certificates and CSR Stores and reads certificates, builds a certificate request for a chip key and checks a chain (requests and chains in the optional PKI layer) StoreCertificate , LoadCertificate , BuildCsr , VerifyChain WriteBinary , ReadObject Supported AN12543 4.7.1.4 WriteBinary, p. 84 Monotonic counters Counters that only count up, for an anti-rollback floor on the firmware version (the facade needs applet 7.x; Device also serves 3.x (AN12413 3.2.1.7, p. 8)) CreateCounter , RaiseCounterTo , CheckFloor , IncrementCounter WriteCounter Supported AN12543 3.2.1.7 Counter, p. 7 Secure channels Platform SCP03 encrypts the bus; AESKey, ECKey and UserID sessions authenticate the caller (ECKey sessions behind a build flag) Open , BeginAesKeySession , BeginEcKeySession , BeginUserIdSession , EndSession CreateSession , SCPInitializeUpdate ( ScpInitializeUpdate ), VerifySessionUserID ( VerifySessionUserId ) Supported AN12543 3.5 Secure Channel Protocols, p. 27 Lifecycle and locks Transport lock, a platform SCP03 requirement and factory reset: one-way changes to the chip (compiled out by default; each needs a plan and a typed confirmation) ExecuteIrreversible , Operations SetLockState , SetPlatformSCPRequest ( SetPlatformScpRequest ), DeleteAll Guarded AN12543 3.8 Lifecycle management, p. 42 Contactless and ISO 7816 The ISO 14443 antenna and ISO 7816 interfaces; the host cannot reach them over I2C - - Not covered SE050 4.2 ISO7816 and ISO14443 interface, p. 9 Supported : the driver covers it and a host test checks it; Guarded : covered, behind an explicit acknowledgement because a wrong value can do harm; Not covered : the chip has it and the driver leaves it alone. From docs/hardware.yml ; kokeb-docs hardware --check confirms that every API name is in inc/se05x_hrot.hpp , inc/se05x_device.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_csr.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_verify.hpp , inc/se05x_pki_device.hpp , inc/se05x_irreversible.hpp and every register (the header constant in brackets, where the header spells it otherwise) in inc/se05x_commands.hpp . The driver has no platform code. You give it small port classes (a bus and a clock, optionally reset and a hardware crypto engine); it does the framing, the secure channel, the checks and the recovery.

docs.text: Provision Keys generated inside the chip, under a strict policy, in one call. Attest Prove a key or a value came from this chip; fresh, verified, typed. Sign and verify ECDSA, and EdDSA except on the SE052F in FIPS mode ( variants ), with keys that never leave the chip. ECDH Key agreement with the secret kept on the chip. Key import Wrapped import under a key-encryption key; no plain key on the host. Secure channels Platform SCP03, AESKey and ECKey sessions; no half-open channel. Secure storage Binary objects whose policy decides who reads them. Certificates Read the provisioned certificates, store your own. Counters Monotonic counters and anti-rollback floors. Lifecycle and lock Transport lock, SCP requirement, factory reset; irreversible steps guarded. Security model What the chip protects, what it does not, and the trust boundaries. Choose a variant SE050, SE051 or SE052, which applet and which authentication.
docs.title: What it does for you

docs.text: Layers with one job each. Link, APDU, secure channel, capability gate, objects, device, facade. See Architecture . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error and the chip's status word. See the API guide . A gate before the bus. A command the chip lacks never reaches it. See Contract . No foot-guns. Irreversible operations are separate types behind named confirmations, compiled out by default. See Safety rules . Honest about doubt. Every open question has a knob. See Ambiguities . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. See Contract . Tested without hardware. The tests run the driver against an independent model of the chip. See Testing and CI .

docs.text: Agent context ¶ What an agent needs before it touches this repository: the flow, the skill for each step, the exact local checks, the file layout, the standing rules, the pitfalls that failed CI before, and when to stop. Read AGENTS.md for the repository itself. This page is managed by the template ( scaffold.py --check-drift --fix ships it) and tools/check_skills.py checks that every skill named here exists and that the files its commands name exist. 1. The flow and the skill for each step ¶ Each step has an input, an output and an exit rule. Do not skip a step and do not start the next before the exit rule holds. # Step Skill Output Exit rule 0 Plan: new driver, extension or duplicate, and the API shape plan-driver placement.md with a verdict Verdict NEW ; otherwise stop or extend 1 Scaffold new-driver-from-template A building driver with the example chip renamed verify passes on the untouched scaffold 2 Build from the datasheet datasheet-conformance , add-driver-feature , add-port Register map, model, tests, driver, port, examples, docs Host tests green; every datasheet topic recorded 3 Self-review cpp20-profile , misra-review , hardware-lessons-review Findings fixed Every catalogue class in recurring-defects.md answered 4 Verify verify Local gate result tools/preflight.sh ends 0 failure(s) 5 Independent review review-round A report per round NO BLOCKER and no MAJOR 6 First-push gate first-push Container rehearsal and the evidence list 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) 7 Publish publish-driver Public repository, one commit, green main , Pages CI gate / gate green on main ; the owner did the owner-only steps 8 Release candidate release Tag v0.1.0-rc.N Release workflow green; checksums verified 9 Hardware hardware-validation Level H0, H1 or H2 stated and evidenced Badge, driver.yml and release text agree 10 After release bump-pin A pin-bump pull request per consumer Consumer CI green A change to an existing driver skips steps 0, 1 and 7: use add-driver-feature or add-port , then steps 3 to 5 and a pull request (AGENTS.md, "Branches, commits and pull requests"). The agent safety-reviewer runs the review skills read-only. 2. The local gate: commands and what passes ¶ Run from the repository root. Set VENV (a venv with the docs theme, lizard, yamllint), CI_TOOLS_DIR (a kokeb-labs/ci-tools checkout) and CLANG_TIDY (version 20) when the tools are not on PATH . A step the preflight skips is named in its last line: install the tool; do not push around it. Command Passes when tools/preflight.sh Last line == 0 failure(s) and no skip you can fix tools/preflight.sh --container 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) (coverage, ASan/UBSan, fuzz in the CI image) python3 tools/scaffold.py --check-drift . no template drift (or each difference is listed under local with a reason) python3 tools/check_standalone.py Exit 0: no other project's name, no dated history, the right copyright holder python3 -I tools/check_skills.py Every skill named in this page exists, has front matter, and names existing files python3 -I tools/check_layout.py One source per header, SDK code only in src/boundary/ python3 -I tools/check_hardware.py driver.yml hardware level, README badge and rig document agree python3 -I tools/check_language.py driver.yml language: block and every place that repeats the C++ standard agree ( --fix rewrites them) python3 tools/misra_lint.py --root . No error; fix warnings in files you touch kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen && kokeb-docs check No diff afterwards ( git diff --exit-code docs README.md ) mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict -d /tmp/site Exit 0, no warning git ls-files | grep -i '\.pdf$' No output git add -A && git ls-files -s examples/esp32/scripts Mode 160000 (a gitlink), if examples/esp32 exists CI-only checks, which a workstation cannot run: the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds. Cover them by reading the misra-review skill and building examples/esp32 with the ESP-IDF version in examples/esp32/app_config.yml (the scripts are in examples/esp32/scripts , Platforms ) when ESP-IDF is installed. Delete the build directories afterwards; never run docker system prune or any other prune on a shared machine. Run one container job at a time and cmake --build ... --parallel 3 at most when other agents are working. 3. File layout ¶ One source per header, same stem. inc/<stem>.hpp has src/<stem>.cpp (or .ipp for a header-only template driver). A header that declares only constants, types, details, registers, the Kconfig defaults or the port contract ( _types , _detail , _registers , _kconfig , _interface ) needs no source. A header with real logic always has its own source. A header that holds only templates, constants or inline types may instead be listed under header_only in tools/layout.yml with a one-line reason (no colon followed by a space in it); nothing else is exempt. No combined file ( a_and_b.cpp ): split it by header. SDK-touching code (ESP-IDF, an RTOS, a vendor HAL) is never in inc/ or in src/ 's logic: it lives one file per SDK component in src/boundary/<component>.cpp , named after the component, so the directory carries the layering rule. A driver normally has none: it reaches hardware only through the port hooks, and the SDK appears only in examples/<platform>/ . The only generated SDK header read by the driver is sdkconfig.h , in inc/<name>_kconfig.hpp . examples/<platform>/ is the only platform code; examples/host/ always exists. Tests do not include SDK headers. Tool configuration is in _config/ only: no copies or symlinks at the root. The root holds only the files AGENTS.md lists. Never commit build*/ , a venv, a PDF, logs or a scratch file. tools/layout.yml (optional) lists the exceptions: header_only , internal , boundary_extra , each with a reason that tools/check_layout.py also keeps current. 4. Naming ¶ Namespace and package are the part number in lower case; files <name>.hpp , <name>_<topic>.hpp ; public methods PascalCase, private camelBack, members snake_case_ , constants kPascalCase , units as suffixes ( TimeoutMs , VoltageMv ); include guards <NAME>_<FILE_STEM>_<EXT> ; enumerations enum class with EnumLast , never a sentinel value; chip-specific Error values from 16. The repository is driver-<part> ; the copyright holder is The driver-<part> authors . Full rules: AGENTS.md and the handbook. 5. Docs and diagrams ¶ Every claim about the chip cites a datasheet section and page; docs/datasheets.yml records vendor, number, revision, date, URL, SHA-256 and one topic per section used. The PDF itself is never committed. docs/hardware.yml is the one description of the chip (package, pins, supply, hooks, blocks, a circuit, the README's overview, capabilities and frames). The pinout, outline, block diagram, wiring and frame figures, the chip card and the coverage table are generated from it and the headers: never draw or type them by hand. The README and docs/index.md lead with the chip (summary, hero figure, capabilities, uses, inside the chip, pins and wiring), then the quick start and the driver coverage; the layering figure is on the architecture page only. Code shown on the site lives in tests/docs/ between --8<-- markers and is compiled. Every public symbol has a Doxygen comment. CHANGELOG.md has ## [Unreleased] with the allowed headings only. A claim of behaviour in docs, comments or the build report names the code and the test that back it (RD-09). Anything only a bench can confirm is marked not verified on hardware with bench steps, and the level is stated ( hardware-validation skill). 6. Standing rules ¶ Stand-alone. The repository describes its own part and nothing else: no product, board, project, person or other repository by name, no lab history, no dates outside release headings, datasheet revisions and waiver expiries. Behaviour learned on a bench is written as the design with its datasheet section. Copyright is The <repo> authors in LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml and the docs footer. Do not put a company or a person there. No attribution. No Co-Authored-By: trailers, "Generated with" footers or tool names in commits, pull requests or files. Commits are signed off ( git commit -s ) with the owner's GitHub noreply address; no personal email address appears anywhere, and security reports go through GitHub advisories ( .github/SECURITY.md ). No secrets (tokens, keys, credentials, personal addresses) and no vendor PDFs or other licensed documents anywhere in the tree, the history, a pull request or a log you attach. Datasheets are fetched only from the vendor's public page into a scratch folder; never bypass a login or a 403, never fetch the same blocked URL again; record the gap and stop that item. Owner-only actions: making a repository public, rulesets and security settings, deleting or recreating a repository, force-pushing, the final release tag. publish-driver lists them. Ask; do not assume. No force-push to main and no history rewrite of a published branch. Never move or delete a tag. Open source references are read for ideas about API shape; no code, table or text is copied from a source whose licence you have not recorded, and none from an unlicensed or copyleft one. Conserve CI. Push only when the local gate passed; push the fixes together; re-run only infrastructure failures ( release skill, section 5). The datasheet is the source of behaviour. When it is silent or contradicts another source, write the design decision and its reason, make the model knob switchable, and list the bench step. Do not change the model to match a bench result without reading the datasheet again. 7. Known pitfalls and the fix ¶ Pitfall Fix The C++ lint job hits its 20-minute limit when the test sources are in the compilation database twice (the unit tests and their optimised copy) or the clang-analyzer runs over every test The preflight times its tidy step and fails over 400 s (a third of the limit). Fix: put the optimised copy ( <name>_optimised_build ) behind a CMake option that the lint workflow turns off, disable clang-analyzer-* for tests/ in tests/.clang-tidy (the analyzer still covers the driver through examples/host ), and keep the suite in few, small translation units The MISRA scan builds with an unbounded make -j and loses the runner on a large tree Give the scan its own small target (headers alone, snippets, examples, fuzz) and bound the job count ( CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=2 ) Local clang-tidy, clang-format or CMake differ from CI Use clang-tidy 20 and clang-format 20 ( CLANG_TIDY , CLANG_FORMAT ); other versions report different findings and a green local run proves nothing ESP-IDF differs between versions (v5.5 is pinned; v6 changes peripheral drivers and error codes, for example an SPI polling transfer accepts only an infinite wait, a bus NACK maps to another error code) Build examples/esp32 with the version in app_config.yml ; use only APIs present in it; do not add an IDF version column without the owner; list every REQUIRES component the example includes MISRA findings on vendor enumerations, esp_err_t values and C naming from an SDK Keep SDK types out of the driver; convert at the edge in src/boundary/<component>.cpp ; use enum class and fixed-width types in the public API A stale deviation marker (a MISRA deviation comment, or a tools/layout.yml / waiver entry) outlives the code it excused Remove the marker in the same commit as the code; the checks fail on an entry that names nothing _u8 / _u16 / _u32 literal operators raise rule 6.9.2 (they take unsigned long long ) Follow the misra-review skill's current pattern for typed constants; do not add new literal operators; ask when unsure An unused named parameter (rule 0.2.2), a discarded std::copy result (0.1.2), char arithmetic (7.0.3), differing parameter names (13.3.3), an else -less chain (9.4.1) Unnamed parameter or static_cast<void> ; static_cast<void>(std::copy(...)) ; compare characters with std::char_traits ; same names in header and definition; final else . tools/misra_lint.py finds most Indirect recursion (8.2.10) between small helpers Draw the call graph of retry and recovery paths; make one function the only caller of the other .gitignore drops a file the build needs ( *.bin silently removes fuzz corpus inputs) Check what git will push, not the working tree: git status --ignored , and git add -A && git ls-files tests/fuzz The host-example CI step runs ./build-example-<cc>/<name>_host_example ; a driver with other example binary names exits 127 after all tests pass Keep the single example target name, or change the workflow input and the preflight together Host builds on macOS cannot see type-width bugs ( %d with int32_t , PRId64 under strict C++20 on newlib, int main(int32_t, ...) ) Compile the sources for a newlib target ( -fsyntax-only ); cast to long long for %lld ; use uint32_t and main(int, char**) Unspecified evaluation order in a check (GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left) Compute the driver result into a local before reading the state it changes (RD-34); tools/eval_order_check.py A clock comparison with half-range logic stops working after 2^31 ms Use unsigned elapsed subtraction ( now - start >= limit ); fuzz with the clock near wrap Container build killed by out-of-memory ( Killed signal terminated program cc1plus ) Pass CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4 or lower to the container; never run two container jobs at once macOS libFuzzer hangs in symbolization and leaves processes behind Set ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 and -print_funcs=0 ; kill orphans afterwards scaffold.py --check-drift fails on .kokeb/template.yml Keep each value on one line; a long description may continue with a trailing \ . Never hand-edit template: A tag was pushed to the wrong commit Do not move or delete it (a ruleset forbids it); cut the next -rc.N and say why Docs figures or generated regions differ between machines Run kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen with the pinned theme version, commit the result, never edit generated regions 8. When to stop and report instead of improvising ¶ Stop, write down what you saw, what you tried and what you need, and hand it back when: the placement verdict is not NEW , or plan-driver ends BLOCKED ; the datasheet cannot be obtained without a login, a bypassed 403 or a licence you cannot confirm, or two datasheet revisions disagree on something the driver depends on; a check fails twice for the same reason and you do not understand the cause, or a CI failure is outside the repository (a shared workflow, a runner, the quota) and is not an infrastructure failure the release skill lists; a fix needs a waiver, a change to a managed file (anything --check-drift ships), a new ESP-IDF version, or a change to kokeb-labs/ci-tools , the handbook or the shared catalogue; an action is owner-only (section 6), irreversible, or touches anything outside this repository; a safety question arises (the chip can switch a load, heat, move or hold a high voltage) that the datasheet does not answer, or a bench result contradicts the datasheet; you find a secret, a vendor PDF, a person's or another project's name already in the tree or the history. An honest "not verified" in the report is worth more than a green check obtained by weakening a test, a lint or a rule. Never do that.

docs.text: Each step has an input, an output and an exit rule. Do not skip a step and do not start the next before the exit rule holds. # Step Skill Output Exit rule 0 Plan: new driver, extension or duplicate, and the API shape plan-driver placement.md with a verdict Verdict NEW ; otherwise stop or extend 1 Scaffold new-driver-from-template A building driver with the example chip renamed verify passes on the untouched scaffold 2 Build from the datasheet datasheet-conformance , add-driver-feature , add-port Register map, model, tests, driver, port, examples, docs Host tests green; every datasheet topic recorded 3 Self-review cpp20-profile , misra-review , hardware-lessons-review Findings fixed Every catalogue class in recurring-defects.md answered 4 Verify verify Local gate result tools/preflight.sh ends 0 failure(s) 5 Independent review review-round A report per round NO BLOCKER and no MAJOR 6 First-push gate first-push Container rehearsal and the evidence list 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) 7 Publish publish-driver Public repository, one commit, green main , Pages CI gate / gate green on main ; the owner did the owner-only steps 8 Release candidate release Tag v0.1.0-rc.N Release workflow green; checksums verified 9 Hardware hardware-validation Level H0, H1 or H2 stated and evidenced Badge, driver.yml and release text agree 10 After release bump-pin A pin-bump pull request per consumer Consumer CI green A change to an existing driver skips steps 0, 1 and 7: use add-driver-feature or add-port , then steps 3 to 5 and a pull request (AGENTS.md, "Branches, commits and pull requests"). The agent safety-reviewer runs the review skills read-only.
docs.title: 1. The flow and the skill for each step

docs.text: Run from the repository root. Set VENV (a venv with the docs theme, lizard, yamllint), CI_TOOLS_DIR (a kokeb-labs/ci-tools checkout) and CLANG_TIDY (version 20) when the tools are not on PATH . A step the preflight skips is named in its last line: install the tool; do not push around it. Command Passes when tools/preflight.sh Last line == 0 failure(s) and no skip you can fix tools/preflight.sh --container 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) (coverage, ASan/UBSan, fuzz in the CI image) python3 tools/scaffold.py --check-drift . no template drift (or each difference is listed under local with a reason) python3 tools/check_standalone.py Exit 0: no other project's name, no dated history, the right copyright holder python3 -I tools/check_skills.py Every skill named in this page exists, has front matter, and names existing files python3 -I tools/check_layout.py One source per header, SDK code only in src/boundary/ python3 -I tools/check_hardware.py driver.yml hardware level, README badge and rig document agree python3 -I tools/check_language.py driver.yml language: block and every place that repeats the C++ standard agree ( --fix rewrites them) python3 tools/misra_lint.py --root . No error; fix warnings in files you touch kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen && kokeb-docs check No diff afterwards ( git diff --exit-code docs README.md ) mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict -d /tmp/site Exit 0, no warning git ls-files | grep -i '\.pdf$' No output git add -A && git ls-files -s examples/esp32/scripts Mode 160000 (a gitlink), if examples/esp32 exists CI-only checks, which a workstation cannot run: the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds. Cover them by reading the misra-review skill and building examples/esp32 with the ESP-IDF version in examples/esp32/app_config.yml (the scripts are in examples/esp32/scripts , Platforms ) when ESP-IDF is installed. Delete the build directories afterwards; never run docker system prune or any other prune on a shared machine. Run one container job at a time and cmake --build ... --parallel 3 at most when other agents are working.
docs.title: 2. The local gate: commands and what passes

docs.text: One source per header, same stem. inc/<stem>.hpp has src/<stem>.cpp (or .ipp for a header-only template driver). A header that declares only constants, types, details, registers, the Kconfig defaults or the port contract ( _types , _detail , _registers , _kconfig , _interface ) needs no source. A header with real logic always has its own source. A header that holds only templates, constants or inline types may instead be listed under header_only in tools/layout.yml with a one-line reason (no colon followed by a space in it); nothing else is exempt. No combined file ( a_and_b.cpp ): split it by header. SDK-touching code (ESP-IDF, an RTOS, a vendor HAL) is never in inc/ or in src/ 's logic: it lives one file per SDK component in src/boundary/<component>.cpp , named after the component, so the directory carries the layering rule. A driver normally has none: it reaches hardware only through the port hooks, and the SDK appears only in examples/<platform>/ . The only generated SDK header read by the driver is sdkconfig.h , in inc/<name>_kconfig.hpp . examples/<platform>/ is the only platform code; examples/host/ always exists. Tests do not include SDK headers. Tool configuration is in _config/ only: no copies or symlinks at the root. The root holds only the files AGENTS.md lists. Never commit build*/ , a venv, a PDF, logs or a scratch file. tools/layout.yml (optional) lists the exceptions: header_only , internal , boundary_extra , each with a reason that tools/check_layout.py also keeps current.
docs.title: 3. File layout

docs.text: Namespace and package are the part number in lower case; files <name>.hpp , <name>_<topic>.hpp ; public methods PascalCase, private camelBack, members snake_case_ , constants kPascalCase , units as suffixes ( TimeoutMs , VoltageMv ); include guards <NAME>_<FILE_STEM>_<EXT> ; enumerations enum class with EnumLast , never a sentinel value; chip-specific Error values from 16. The repository is driver-<part> ; the copyright holder is The driver-<part> authors . Full rules: AGENTS.md and the handbook.
docs.title: 4. Naming

docs.text: Every claim about the chip cites a datasheet section and page; docs/datasheets.yml records vendor, number, revision, date, URL, SHA-256 and one topic per section used. The PDF itself is never committed. docs/hardware.yml is the one description of the chip (package, pins, supply, hooks, blocks, a circuit, the README's overview, capabilities and frames). The pinout, outline, block diagram, wiring and frame figures, the chip card and the coverage table are generated from it and the headers: never draw or type them by hand. The README and docs/index.md lead with the chip (summary, hero figure, capabilities, uses, inside the chip, pins and wiring), then the quick start and the driver coverage; the layering figure is on the architecture page only. Code shown on the site lives in tests/docs/ between --8<-- markers and is compiled. Every public symbol has a Doxygen comment. CHANGELOG.md has ## [Unreleased] with the allowed headings only. A claim of behaviour in docs, comments or the build report names the code and the test that back it (RD-09). Anything only a bench can confirm is marked not verified on hardware with bench steps, and the level is stated ( hardware-validation skill).
docs.title: 5. Docs and diagrams

docs.text: Stand-alone. The repository describes its own part and nothing else: no product, board, project, person or other repository by name, no lab history, no dates outside release headings, datasheet revisions and waiver expiries. Behaviour learned on a bench is written as the design with its datasheet section. Copyright is The <repo> authors in LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml and the docs footer. Do not put a company or a person there. No attribution. No Co-Authored-By: trailers, "Generated with" footers or tool names in commits, pull requests or files. Commits are signed off ( git commit -s ) with the owner's GitHub noreply address; no personal email address appears anywhere, and security reports go through GitHub advisories ( .github/SECURITY.md ). No secrets (tokens, keys, credentials, personal addresses) and no vendor PDFs or other licensed documents anywhere in the tree, the history, a pull request or a log you attach. Datasheets are fetched only from the vendor's public page into a scratch folder; never bypass a login or a 403, never fetch the same blocked URL again; record the gap and stop that item. Owner-only actions: making a repository public, rulesets and security settings, deleting or recreating a repository, force-pushing, the final release tag. publish-driver lists them. Ask; do not assume. No force-push to main and no history rewrite of a published branch. Never move or delete a tag. Open source references are read for ideas about API shape; no code, table or text is copied from a source whose licence you have not recorded, and none from an unlicensed or copyleft one. Conserve CI. Push only when the local gate passed; push the fixes together; re-run only infrastructure failures ( release skill, section 5). The datasheet is the source of behaviour. When it is silent or contradicts another source, write the design decision and its reason, make the model knob switchable, and list the bench step. Do not change the model to match a bench result without reading the datasheet again.
docs.title: 6. Standing rules

docs.text: Pitfall Fix The C++ lint job hits its 20-minute limit when the test sources are in the compilation database twice (the unit tests and their optimised copy) or the clang-analyzer runs over every test The preflight times its tidy step and fails over 400 s (a third of the limit). Fix: put the optimised copy ( <name>_optimised_build ) behind a CMake option that the lint workflow turns off, disable clang-analyzer-* for tests/ in tests/.clang-tidy (the analyzer still covers the driver through examples/host ), and keep the suite in few, small translation units The MISRA scan builds with an unbounded make -j and loses the runner on a large tree Give the scan its own small target (headers alone, snippets, examples, fuzz) and bound the job count ( CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=2 ) Local clang-tidy, clang-format or CMake differ from CI Use clang-tidy 20 and clang-format 20 ( CLANG_TIDY , CLANG_FORMAT ); other versions report different findings and a green local run proves nothing ESP-IDF differs between versions (v5.5 is pinned; v6 changes peripheral drivers and error codes, for example an SPI polling transfer accepts only an infinite wait, a bus NACK maps to another error code) Build examples/esp32 with the version in app_config.yml ; use only APIs present in it; do not add an IDF version column without the owner; list every REQUIRES component the example includes MISRA findings on vendor enumerations, esp_err_t values and C naming from an SDK Keep SDK types out of the driver; convert at the edge in src/boundary/<component>.cpp ; use enum class and fixed-width types in the public API A stale deviation marker (a MISRA deviation comment, or a tools/layout.yml / waiver entry) outlives the code it excused Remove the marker in the same commit as the code; the checks fail on an entry that names nothing _u8 / _u16 / _u32 literal operators raise rule 6.9.2 (they take unsigned long long ) Follow the misra-review skill's current pattern for typed constants; do not add new literal operators; ask when unsure An unused named parameter (rule 0.2.2), a discarded std::copy result (0.1.2), char arithmetic (7.0.3), differing parameter names (13.3.3), an else -less chain (9.4.1) Unnamed parameter or static_cast<void> ; static_cast<void>(std::copy(...)) ; compare characters with std::char_traits ; same names in header and definition; final else . tools/misra_lint.py finds most Indirect recursion (8.2.10) between small helpers Draw the call graph of retry and recovery paths; make one function the only caller of the other .gitignore drops a file the build needs ( *.bin silently removes fuzz corpus inputs) Check what git will push, not the working tree: git status --ignored , and git add -A && git ls-files tests/fuzz The host-example CI step runs ./build-example-<cc>/<name>_host_example ; a driver with other example binary names exits 127 after all tests pass Keep the single example target name, or change the workflow input and the preflight together Host builds on macOS cannot see type-width bugs ( %d with int32_t , PRId64 under strict C++20 on newlib, int main(int32_t, ...) ) Compile the sources for a newlib target ( -fsyntax-only ); cast to long long for %lld ; use uint32_t and main(int, char**) Unspecified evaluation order in a check (GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left) Compute the driver result into a local before reading the state it changes (RD-34); tools/eval_order_check.py A clock comparison with half-range logic stops working after 2^31 ms Use unsigned elapsed subtraction ( now - start >= limit ); fuzz with the clock near wrap Container build killed by out-of-memory ( Killed signal terminated program cc1plus ) Pass CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4 or lower to the container; never run two container jobs at once macOS libFuzzer hangs in symbolization and leaves processes behind Set ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 and -print_funcs=0 ; kill orphans afterwards scaffold.py --check-drift fails on .kokeb/template.yml Keep each value on one line; a long description may continue with a trailing \ . Never hand-edit template: A tag was pushed to the wrong commit Do not move or delete it (a ruleset forbids it); cut the next -rc.N and say why Docs figures or generated regions differ between machines Run kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen with the pinned theme version, commit the result, never edit generated regions
docs.title: 7. Known pitfalls and the fix

docs.text: Stop, write down what you saw, what you tried and what you need, and hand it back when: the placement verdict is not NEW , or plan-driver ends BLOCKED ; the datasheet cannot be obtained without a login, a bypassed 403 or a licence you cannot confirm, or two datasheet revisions disagree on something the driver depends on; a check fails twice for the same reason and you do not understand the cause, or a CI failure is outside the repository (a shared workflow, a runner, the quota) and is not an infrastructure failure the release skill lists; a fix needs a waiver, a change to a managed file (anything --check-drift ships), a new ESP-IDF version, or a change to kokeb-labs/ci-tools , the handbook or the shared catalogue; an action is owner-only (section 6), irreversible, or touches anything outside this repository; a safety question arises (the chip can switch a load, heat, move or hold a high voltage) that the datasheet does not answer, or a bench result contradicts the datasheet; you find a secret, a vendor PDF, a person's or another project's name already in the tree or the history. An honest "not verified" in the report is worth more than a green check obtained by weakening a test, a lint or a rule. Never do that.
docs.title: 8. When to stop and report instead of improvising

anything else is PolicyDenied (fails closed: a chip that reformats the policy would make adoption fail, never pass) none provision a facade key, then ReadObjectAttributes it on a dev kit and compare the policy with the one sent A35 A store cut short by a power loss partly: AN12543 does not say whether one WriteBinary is atomic or what a new binary file holds before it is written Store creates the object one byte longer than the data and writes a completion marker (0xA5) after every data chunk, by its own command; Load and Attest refuse an object without it. A new file that the chip does not zero-fill could hold 0xA5 there by chance (1 in 256). An object not written by Store is FrameError , or, if its last byte is 0xA5, reads back one byte short none cut the power during a 700-byte Store on a dev kit 20 times at random points; Load must return FrameError or the whole value every time A36 Attested read of an object above the 500-byte chunk limit open: AN13030 (pp. 248-252) limits one attested binary read to 500 bytes, and does not say what the chip answers to a read without offset and length of a larger object Attest reads the object whole into a 256-byte buffer ( kMaxAttestedBytes ); the model returns the whole value, which the host refuses as BufferTooSmall . A chip that answers an error status instead returns that status's error (a device error, not BufferTooSmall ); either way no value is returned model only ( kMaxBinary ) Store 255, 300 and 600 bytes on a dev kit, Attest each, and record the error and the status word of each ( Device::GetLastStatusWord() ) Corrections folded into the contract ¶ A quiet chip answers within about 20 s, and up to 40 WTX requests are answered at session open. The old reference of 500 WTX is gone; Config::wtx_limit and kSessionOpenWtxAllowance carry the numbers. GetFreeMemory returns 4 bytes on the SE052F only and 2 bytes elsewhere, SE051 7.x included. SIGMA-I is not an SE05x feature. It is not in the command set. Ed25519 and Montgomery values on the wire are the byte reverse of RFC 8032 and RFC 7748 (AN12543 pp. 168-170; an earlier note said little endian, which AN12543 corrects). A Montgomery ECDH with an inline public key writes NVM on every call. On the SE050 and SE051, RST_N is the ISO 7816 reset and has no effect when only I2C is enabled (SE050 section 4.2, p. 9): there the reset port implements Reset() and PowerCycle() with ENA (VOUT wired to VCC) or a supply switch; the link only calls the port. Still open ¶ UM11225 was obtained (addendum 3). Both T=1 flavours are specified except the CRC byte order of the NXP flavour: the link accepts either order on the first valid frame and keeps it (A10). The code 0xC6 is a chip reset in the NXP flavour and RELEASE in the GP one. The GP flavour is specified by GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, but the SE052 data sheet selects a "GP 0.39" flavour, and the NAD and MPOT unit the chips use in it are open (A17, A32). The ECKey KDF is printed in AN12543 pp. 22-23 and 72-73 but has no vector: it is built behind a feature flag. The order of the attestation timestamp is settled (AN12543 3.9, p. 42: 4 persistent bytes, then 8 transient bytes, growing with every session open); the driver accepts only a timestamp later than the last one it accepted. The 6.x policy bit values, the SE052 configuration sheet and the SOT917 code stay open. The SEMS Lite update agent is outside v1. Oracle vectors from the vendor middleware ¶ tests/vectors/nxp_oracle_vectors.hpp holds vectors recorded by tools/oracle/build_oracle.sh against the pinned middleware checkout 7102413e , in a sandbox without network access (provenance and the BSD 3-Clause notice in tests/vectors/THIRD_PARTY.md ). It records 122 commands, 62 on applet 7.2 and 60 on applet 3.x. tests/test_apdu_oracle_vectors.cpp builds each command with the same inputs and compares header and TLV body byte for byte; every remaining difference is listed there with its class and evidence (middleware quirks such as TAG_11 version 0 and TAG_2 FF ; policy-less creates, which the library refuses, S-03; the WriteUserID instruction byte of the harness input; DeleteAll , below), and removing any one of them makes the test fail. The TLSPerformPRF P2 is no longer a difference: TlsPrfArgs::role gives the server role (AN12543 4.17.3), which the harness used. Framing is not compared: the middleware frames short case 4 without Le and extended commands as 00 LcH LcL ... 00 00 . The structural check of tests/vectors/nxp_layouts.hpp (read from the source text by tools/oracle/extract_layouts.py ) remains. The oracle covers 122 of the commands; the others rest on the APDU tables of AN12543 and AN12413 only. The ECKey key derivation, receipt and first MAC chaining value still rest on the independent chip model only (A15): that session stays behind its build flag. DeleteAll: Lc 0x00 or case 1 ¶ AN12543 Table 339 prints the DeleteAll command with Lc 0x00 , so the codec sends 80 04 00 2A 00 ; the middleware sends case 1 ( 80 04 00 2A , four bytes). Read as ISO/IEC 7816-4 the trailing byte is an Le, which the chip ignores for a command without a response, so both should be accepted. Not verified on hardware : a trace of DeleteAll on a real chip (bench step: run it in a RESERVED_ID_FACTORY_RESET session on a dev kit and record the C-APDU and the status word) decides it. Attested read under secure messaging ¶ A format 2 attestation signs the hash of "the complete APDU except the Le bytes" (AN12543 3.2.7.2, p. 19). Inside platform SCP03 or an AESKey session the applet sees the command after the secure channel unwrapped it, and the documents do not say which length form it then hashes. The driver hashes the unwrapped command with the shortest Lc form (one byte for up to 255 bytes, no Le), which is how the chip model rebuilds a command after unwrapping; outside secure messaging it hashes the command exactly as sent ( Device::ReadVerified , detail::ShortestLcForm ). A wrong choice fails closed: every attestation is refused with AttestationInvalid , nothing false is accepted. Not verified on hardware : bench step: run hrot::Device::Attest() under platform SCP03 on a dev kit; if it fails while the same read without secure messaging passes, the chip hashes the extended form.

docs.text: A quiet chip answers within about 20 s, and up to 40 WTX requests are answered at session open. The old reference of 500 WTX is gone; Config::wtx_limit and kSessionOpenWtxAllowance carry the numbers. GetFreeMemory returns 4 bytes on the SE052F only and 2 bytes elsewhere, SE051 7.x included. SIGMA-I is not an SE05x feature. It is not in the command set. Ed25519 and Montgomery values on the wire are the byte reverse of RFC 8032 and RFC 7748 (AN12543 pp. 168-170; an earlier note said little endian, which AN12543 corrects). A Montgomery ECDH with an inline public key writes NVM on every call. On the SE050 and SE051, RST_N is the ISO 7816 reset and has no effect when only I2C is enabled (SE050 section 4.2, p. 9): there the reset port implements Reset() and PowerCycle() with ENA (VOUT wired to VCC) or a supply switch; the link only calls the port.
docs.title: Corrections folded into the contract

docs.text: UM11225 was obtained (addendum 3). Both T=1 flavours are specified except the CRC byte order of the NXP flavour: the link accepts either order on the first valid frame and keeps it (A10). The code 0xC6 is a chip reset in the NXP flavour and RELEASE in the GP one. The GP flavour is specified by GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, but the SE052 data sheet selects a "GP 0.39" flavour, and the NAD and MPOT unit the chips use in it are open (A17, A32). The ECKey KDF is printed in AN12543 pp. 22-23 and 72-73 but has no vector: it is built behind a feature flag. The order of the attestation timestamp is settled (AN12543 3.9, p. 42: 4 persistent bytes, then 8 transient bytes, growing with every session open); the driver accepts only a timestamp later than the last one it accepted. The 6.x policy bit values, the SE052 configuration sheet and the SOT917 code stay open. The SEMS Lite update agent is outside v1.

A call returns Result : check .ok() before using the value. using BoardPorts = se05x :: Ports < MyBus , MyClock , se05x :: ReferenceCrypto > ; se05x :: Error RandomBytes ( MyBus & bus , MyClock & clock , se05x :: ReferenceCrypto & crypto , se05x :: MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { const BoardPorts ports ( bus , clock , crypto ); se05x :: Device < BoardPorts > device ( ports , se05x :: Config {}); if ( const auto opened = device . Open (); ! opened . ok ()) { return opened . error ; // for example DeviceIdMismatch: nothing answered like an SE05x } const auto random = device . GetRandom ( out ); static_cast < void > ( device . Close ()); return random . error ; } Open() does the boot wait, the ATR or CIP, the resynchronisation, the applet select and the version read. Handle errors ¶ Error What to do NotInitialized Call Open() Unsupported The chip lacks the command; check GetCapabilities() WrongState Open the session or authenticate first; see Role() Nack , Timeout , Crc The link retries; a persistent one climbs the recovery ladder Resynced , NeedsReselect Re-authenticate or select again, then repeat the command yourself BusStuck , TransportDead Call PowerCycle() when the reset port exists ThroughputLimited The chip limits APDUs (SW 0x66A6); wait, then the ladder ends in a chip reset ( S-17 ) PolicyDenied , AuthLocked The object policy or the attempt limit; no retry helps IrreversibleNotConfirmed An irreversible operation lacked its Confirmation GetLastStatusWord() and GetLastDetail() give the chip's status word and the layer that failed. Close ¶ Close() ends the sessions and leaves the chip selectable; DeepPowerDown() puts it into its lowest-current state when the core supply comes from VOUT.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: layers with one owner each, ports at the bottom, and what happens in each when you open the device. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7: Timeouts and waiting time extensions: 2.10, p. 9 APDU throughput limit, SW 0x66A6: 2.12 and 10.16.6, p. 10 ECKey session flow and receipt: ECKey session, p. 156 T=1 chip reset and deep power-down: 10.16, p. 281 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/se05x_device.hpp public calls ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Header Job Ports se05x_ports.hpp Bus, clock, crypto, optional reset and log; CRTP, checked by concepts T=1 link se05x_t1.hpp , se05x_atr.hpp Framing, CRC, WTX, the recovery ladder (resend, resync, interface reset, reselect, chip reset, power cycle) APDU and TLV se05x_apdu*.hpp Builders and parsers; the status word map Secure channels se05x_scp03.hpp , se05x_eckey.hpp , se05x_gp.hpp SCP03, ECKey sessions, GlobalPlatform commands Capability gate se05x_gate.hpp , se05x_caps.hpp Refuses what the chip cannot do before it reaches the bus Objects and policies se05x_objects.hpp , se05x_policy.hpp Typed ids, classes and generation-typed policy bits Device se05x_device.hpp Execute<C> over 105 commands, lifecycle, sessions Facade se05x_hrot.hpp Slots, key handles, identity, attestation, the APDU budget A bad frame is retried by the link; a lost chip climbs the ladder. A reset closes every session, so each rung drops all session knowledge. The chip's throughput limit (SW 0x66A6) maps to ThroughputLimited and ends in a chip reset. Test model ¶ The tests do not use the NXP middleware. A chain T1Target -> ScpTarget -> ChipModel implements ApduHandler ( tests/model/model_if.hpp ) and is written from the data sheets and application notes, with knobs for the open questions ( Ambiguities ).
docs.title: Architecture

docs.text: How the driver is built: layers with one owner each, ports at the bottom, and what happens in each when you open the device. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7: Timeouts and waiting time extensions: 2.10, p. 9 APDU throughput limit, SW 0x66A6: 2.12 and 10.16.6, p. 10 ECKey session flow and receipt: ECKey session, p. 156 T=1 chip reset and deep power-down: 10.16, p. 281 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/se05x_device.hpp public calls ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py .

docs.text: Layer Header Job Ports se05x_ports.hpp Bus, clock, crypto, optional reset and log; CRTP, checked by concepts T=1 link se05x_t1.hpp , se05x_atr.hpp Framing, CRC, WTX, the recovery ladder (resend, resync, interface reset, reselect, chip reset, power cycle) APDU and TLV se05x_apdu*.hpp Builders and parsers; the status word map Secure channels se05x_scp03.hpp , se05x_eckey.hpp , se05x_gp.hpp SCP03, ECKey sessions, GlobalPlatform commands Capability gate se05x_gate.hpp , se05x_caps.hpp Refuses what the chip cannot do before it reaches the bus Objects and policies se05x_objects.hpp , se05x_policy.hpp Typed ids, classes and generation-typed policy bits Device se05x_device.hpp Execute<C> over 105 commands, lifecycle, sessions Facade se05x_hrot.hpp Slots, key handles, identity, attestation, the APDU budget A bad frame is retried by the link; a lost chip climbs the ladder. A reset closes every session, so each rung drops all session knowledge. The chip's throughput limit (SW 0x66A6) maps to ThroughputLimited and ends in a chip reset.

Mutation catalogues per area ( tools/mutants/transport.txt , apdu.txt , channels.txt , run with --catalogue or --all ) and a core set of each in mutants.py ; mutants run with the library's bounds checks and a timeout. wire::kEddsaInputMax (940) and wire::kEddsaInputMaxUserId (919), with wire::EddsaInputMax() ; the CTest se05x_eckey_on (the ECKey session with its build flag on). Device

: Open() (card identification, select, extended features, probes, ReadState , capabilities, platform SCP03 by Config::scp_policy ), Close() , Recover() , PowerCycle() , DeepPowerDown() , the UserID, AESKey and ECKey sessions (the ECKey one only after ReadEckaPublicKey() verified the chip's key by attestation), Execute() for every reversible command through the gate, the role check, the policy generation check and the EdDSA and UserID limits, ExecuteIrreversible() with its typed state checks, the 0x66A6 reset ladder (one chip reset per call), raw lab access and the named wrappers; the transport stack runs an applet session inside platform SCP03 ( se05x_device_stage.hpp ) and never falls back to the plain link once platform SCP03 was open. Device::SetPlatformKeys() , Device::ReadEckaPublicKey() , AuthRole::Restrict , TlsPrfArgs::role (the TLS server role of TLSPerformPRF ), kMaxPlainCommandApdu . The independent chip model tests/model/chip_model.hpp (profiles SE050, SE050E, SE051, SE052F) and the bench tests/model/chip_bench.hpp ; device tests, the flag-on executable se05x_device_irreversible_on , the sequence fuzzer fuzz_device_sequence and the mutation catalogue tools/mutants/device.txt . The root-of-trust facade hrot::Device

: typed slots per kind, keys typed by use, Provision() , Find() , GetPublicKey() , Sign() , TlsSign() , VerifySignature() (fails closed), Agree() , ImportPublicKey() , Attest() returning Verified , stored data and certificates, monotonic counters with CheckFloor() and RaiseCounterTo() , Random() , the APDU budget (S-17) with SetWindowCount() ; every key, counter and secret-data call needs secure messaging. Compile-fail tests for each foot-gun (wrong slot kind, wrong key use, a forged key or verified value, an out-of-range slot, a generated verification key, a confirmation of another operation). irreversible::Operations

: plans and Apply() for the persistent lock, the platform SCP03 requirement, the applet features, DeleteAll , the object-creation restriction, an immutable object and a finite authentication object; the four operations this version cannot do are refused at the plan. Device::ReadVerified() : an attested read verified in one call. Compiled job snippets for every path of the getting-started page and the cookbook ( tests/docs/jobs.hpp , lifecycle.hpp ), run against the chip model; the host example runs the facade jobs on the simulated chip; the ESP32 facade example; the optional PSA crypto port ( examples/psa/ ); the mutation catalogue tools/mutants/hrot.txt ; the facade sequence fuzzer fuzz_hrot_sequence . The optional PKI layer se05x::pki ( se05x_pki.hpp , opt-in): a strict DER reader and a DER writer, PKCS#10 requests signed by a chip key ( DeviceSigner ) or a crypto-port key ( PortSigner ) with subject and subjectAltName builders, a strict X.509 v3 parser, chain verification to caller-supplied trust anchors (ECDSA P-256 and P-384 through a verifier port, caller-supplied time, path length), certificate and trust-anchor storage in read-only binary objects, the provisioning recipes, OpenSSL test vectors, the fuzz targets fuzz_pki_der and fuzz_pki_x509 , the mutation catalogue tools/mutants/pki.txt , the page docs/pki.md and its figure. Layer::Pki : the layer of a PKI refusal, whose Detail::step is the pki::Reason . Safety behaviour of the first version: attested reads take a host nonce and accept only a later timestamp, across reopens; the facade's counters cannot be deleted and are created with their value; facade calls need authenticated answers (keys, counters, verification) or encryption both ways (ECDH, secret data); facade policies name the applet session they are made in; Find() and CreateCounter() adopt only a persistent object of the right class and origin with the facade's exact policy; ECDH peers and trust anchors must be points on P-256; immutable files and UserID objects only through the irreversible operations; the APDU count spans every open, counts every session handshake APDU and saturates; Store() writes a completion marker last and Load() and Attest() refuse an object without it; every facade call is admitted on its worst-case APDU count before the first APDU ( hrot::cost , shown in the HRoT cookbook and checked by the CTest se05x_docs_costs ); the facade runs on applet 7.x only and refuses 3.x and 6.x with Unsupported before sending. Transport behaviour: a WTX extends any command to at least 4 s, one WTX grants at most 30 s and the WTX of one command at most 180 s; a BWT above 10 s is refused; the guard time holds before every read and write; 300 us of quiet after an SE052 deep power-down by S-block; Auto tries the NXP flavour first, and the GP flavour accepts NAD 0xA5 from the chip. Documentation: ambiguities A1 to A36, each with a bench step; the datasheet map in docs/datasheets.yml ; the hardware description in docs/hardware.yml . APDU budget after SW 0x66A6: the recovery (select, ReadState , the platform SCP03 handshake) may send up to four APDUs beyond a facade call's admitted cost, counted in Used() ; Store sends no clean-up delete after ThroughputLimited . Claim C8, S-17 and the cost table say so, and a test pins the bound. Ambiguity A36 (attested read of an object above the 500-byte chunk limit), with a bench step. Facade refusals on older applets and short reads: the documents say applet 3.x and 6.x (every facade call returns Unsupported there after its argument checks; claim C13), with the model profile se051_v6 , a test of every facade call on both generations and a test that the argument checks run first; Attest and Load are tested against a value cut short under a valid signature (model knob read_truncate ), and the store-marker check directly, including a signed size above the 256-byte buffer. Changed ¶ Each command codec is a struct in se05x::codecs , selected by an overload codecs::CodecFor(CommandTag) ; Codec keeps its interface, and its only specialisation is in se05x_codec.hpp (MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.3). A two- or three-argument Decode that does not fill its reply takes it by const reference. The Name and AltNames entries are pki::detail::NameEntry and AltNameEntry , no longer nested types. The facade's key and slot parameters name Key and SlotOf ; the aliases ( SignKey , DataSlot , ...) stay for callers. Fixed ¶ A host test read the command count in the same call that sent a command, so its result depended on the order in which the compiler evaluated arguments. Test code no longer passes a null pointer with a length of zero to memcpy or memcmp ( tests/model/bytes.hpp ). SHA helpers index spans instead of doing pointer arithmetic (Rule 8.7.1); checkArgs names its unused flag.

docs.text: Claims and their limits ¶ Every security claim the guides make, with the condition it needs, what it does not cover, and the host test that checks it against the chip model. The CTest se05x_docs_claims fails when a test named here no longer exists, so a claim cannot quietly outgrow the code. None of these is verified on hardware yet; the bench steps are on each guide and on Ambiguities . Id Claim Holds when Does not cover Test C1 Facade calls on keys, counters and signature verification are refused unless answers are authenticated (R-MAC), with nothing sent always Attest , which needs no R-MAC because it checks the chip's own signature, and a C-MAC-only channel, which authenticates commands but not answers Integrity: platform SCP03 at C-MAC only answers nothing the facade trusts C2 Store / Load with Protection::Secret , and Agree , are refused unless traffic is encrypted both ways the caller passes Protection::Secret for a secret object Load(..., Protection::Public) of a secret object over a channel without R-ENC (for example CMacCDecrypt ) reads it unencrypted: always pass the protection the object was stored with Integrity: C-MAC and R-MAC admits keys and counters, not secrets C3 A counter floor cannot be lowered or deleted and re-created lower the counter was made by CreateCounter a factory reset, which removes it Integrity: the floor cannot be lowered by delete and re-create C4 Find and CreateCounter adopt only a persistent object of the right class and origin with the facade's exact policy the chip returns the policy as written (A34) a Sign and a TlsClient key, whose policies are the same Integrity: the adoption check compares class, origin, policy and lifetime each on its own C5 A store cut short is never read back as a value the chip does not leave 0xA5 in an unwritten byte (A35) the object stays until erased Integrity: a store cut short before its completion marker is never read back as data C6 A replayed or older attested answer is refused the trusted attestation key is genuine a server: the check runs on the host only Facade: a replayed attested answer is refused (host nonce, strict timestamp order) C7 An ECDH peer that is not on P-256 is refused before sending always the peer's identity: authenticate the peer key yourself Guards: a peer or trust anchor that is not on P-256 is refused before sending C8 A facade call is admitted only when its worst-case APDU count fits under the ceiling, so an answered call never passes it, and the count spans reopens and session handshakes one Device object per chip the recovery after a 0x66A6 answer, which sends up to four APDUs past the admitted cost (select, lifecycle read, platform SCP03 handshake), counted in Used() and tested as that bound, and APDUs sent by se05x::Device calls you make directly, which are counted but not admitted Guards: every facade path stays within its admitted cost at the budget's edge , Guards: a 0x66A6 answer at the edge passes the ceiling by at most the four recovery APDUs C9 One WTX grants at most 30 s and the WTX of one command at most 180 s always the time before the first WTX (the command class deadline) One WTX grants at most 30 s, and the WTX of one command at most 180 s in all C10 The bare 9000 of a session-ending command is accepted once, for that command only the command is DeleteAll in an applet session that answer is not authenticated (A22) A bare 9000 is accepted once after ExpectSessionEnd, never on a later answer C11 Facade policies name the default session and the applet session they were made in id 0 is the default session only (A20) other sessions: the chip refuses them Integrity: a facade policy names the AESKey session it is created in (A20) C12 Once platform SCP03 was open, the device sends no applet command in the clear until Recover() or Open() , which redo the handshake plain commands a probe sends itself before RequirePlatformScp (see Security model ) Sessions: the applet stage never sends in the clear once platform SCP03 is required C13 The facade refuses applet 3.x and 6.x before sending anything always, after the argument checks the device layer, which works on 3.x and 6.x Facade: applet 3.x and 6.x are refused before anything is sent C14 A facade counter cannot be lowered, deleted or re-created lower the counter was made by CreateCounter raising it: a host holding the platform SCP03 keys or the session credential can raise it to 0xFFFFFFFF, which blocks every later update (a denial of service, see Anti-rollback ) Integrity: the floor cannot be lowered by delete and re-create

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every field of se05x::Config , how a configuration is checked, and the optional Kconfig layer. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7: Timeouts and waiting time extensions: 2.10, p. 9 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Fields ¶ Config{} holds safe defaults, and Validate() rejects an out-of-range value before anything is sent. Field Default Meaning i2c_address kI2cAddress (0x48) 7-bit address boot_wait_ms 20 Wait before the first frame (ambiguity A8); 0 is valid atr_poll_budget_ms 1000 How long to poll for the ATR or CIP; must be above 0 frame_retries kDefaultFrameRetries (3) T=1 retries per frame wtx_limit kDefaultWtxLimit (64) Waiting time extensions per command; kSessionOpenWtxAllowance (40) applies at session open flavour Auto T=1 framing flavour: the NXP form first, then GP (ambiguities A9, A17) timeouts class defaults Per command class (ambiguity A11); a WTX extends any class to at least 4 s (A19) poll_interval_us 1000 Polling period of a chip that NAKs until ready; 1 ms to 1 s scp_policy Auto Platform SCP03: Auto opens it when the chip requires it, Require always, Off never. Auto decides from the chip's answer to ReadState, which is not authenticated, so a host on the bus can make it skip platform SCP03; the facade then refuses keys, counters and secrets (it fails closed). Set Require for a root of trust auth_attempt_limit 3 Host-side authentication attempts per session (S-14) probe_capabilities true Probe digest support and the curve list at Open() (A4, A5) verify_eckey_receipt true Check the ECKey session receipt (A15); it cannot be turned off by a call allow_lab_override false Lab only: let TransmitRaw() bypass the capability gate held_commands empty Commands refused as Unsupported before sending (A6) The SCL clock is the bus port's, not a Config field: keep it at or below kMaxClockHz (a port can check its own setting with static_assert , as the ESP-IDF example does). Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig has a "SE05X secure element" menu: CONFIG_SE05X_BOOT_WAIT_MS , ATR_POLL_BUDGET_MS , FRAME_RETRIES , SCP_REQUIRE or SCP_OFF , PROBE_DISABLE , and SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE (default off). se05x::KconfigDefaults() returns the result and equals Config{} when nothing is changed. Outside ESP-IDF the CMake option SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE sets the same flag. docs.text: Config{} holds safe defaults, and Validate() rejects an out-of-range value before anything is sent. Field Default Meaning i2c_address kI2cAddress (0x48) 7-bit address boot_wait_ms 20 Wait before the first frame (ambiguity A8); 0 is valid atr_poll_budget_ms 1000 How long to poll for the ATR or CIP; must be above 0 frame_retries kDefaultFrameRetries (3) T=1 retries per frame wtx_limit kDefaultWtxLimit (64) Waiting time extensions per command; kSessionOpenWtxAllowance (40) applies at session open flavour Auto T=1 framing flavour: the NXP form first, then GP (ambiguities A9, A17) timeouts class defaults Per command class (ambiguity A11); a WTX extends any class to at least 4 s (A19) poll_interval_us 1000 Polling period of a chip that NAKs until ready; 1 ms to 1 s scp_policy Auto Platform SCP03: Auto opens it when the chip requires it, Require always, Off never. Auto decides from the chip's answer to ReadState, which is not authenticated, so a host on the bus can make it skip platform SCP03; the facade then refuses keys, counters and secrets (it fails closed). Set Require for a root of trust auth_attempt_limit 3 Host-side authentication attempts per session (S-14) probe_capabilities true Probe digest support and the curve list at Open() (A4, A5) verify_eckey_receipt true Check the ECKey session receipt (A15); it cannot be turned off by a call allow_lab_override false Lab only: let TransmitRaw() bypass the capability gate held_commands empty Commands refused as Unsupported before sending (A6) The SCL clock is the bus port's, not a Config field: keep it at or below kMaxClockHz (a port can check its own setting with static_assert , as the ESP-IDF example does).
