docs.text:
Contract ¶ What the SE05x driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . The public headers in inc/ are frozen: a change to a signature updates the compile-only contract test ( tests/test_contract.cpp ) in the same change. Promises ¶ Device::Open() is the only way to start the driver. It waits for the chip, reads the ATR or CIP, resynchronises the T=1 link, selects the applet, reads the version and fills Capabilities . On any failure the device stays closed and the next call starts again from the beginning. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before Open() succeeds. No call opens or resets the chip as a side effect. Every command is checked by the capability gate (generation, applet version, features, lock and platform SCP state), by the lifecycle role check, by the policy's applet generation and by the limits the codec cannot see (the 919-byte EdDSA input of a UserID session, the UserID credential rules) before any byte goes on the bus. A refusal is Unsupported , WrongState , ConditionsNotSatisfied , PolicyInvalid or InvalidArgument and costs no round trip. Once platform SCP03 is open, no applet command goes out in the clear until Close() ; a lost platform channel leaves the device NeedsReopen until Recover() opens it again. SW 0x66A6 resets the chip once per call and never repeats the command ( ThroughputLimited ). Every port failure propagates; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. Every wait is bounded by Config::timeouts , wtx_limit and frame_retries . Secrets live in Secret and KeyHandle types, are wiped on destruction and are never logged. An irreversible operation is a distinct type behind a named Confirmation , and is compiled out unless the build sets SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE ( Safety rules ). Every layer is built: the device ( Device

), the facade ( hrot::Device

) and the irreversible plans ( irreversible::Operations

). No call returns Error::NotImplemented any more; the contract test pins every signature. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the ports CMake 3.16 or later Generates se05x_version.h Your ports A bus (I2C, 7-bit address 0x48, up to 400 kHz here), a clock; optionally reset, log and a hardware crypto port Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. The NXP Plug & Trust middleware is a test oracle in the tools, never a dependency. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. One command is in flight at a time (errata I2C.1): use each device from one task, or guard every call with one mutex. Nothing may run in an ISR. Separate devices share no state. Errors ¶ se05x::Error inside se05x::Result . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; 16 and up are chip specific. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Open() has not succeeded, or Close() ran since InvalidArgument 2 An argument or Config field is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 The I2C port failed Timeout 4 A bounded wait ended DeviceIdMismatch 5 The chip is not the expected family or applet Crc 6 A T=1 frame failed its CRC16 and the retry budget is spent Busy 7 A command is in flight DeviceFault 8 The chip reported an internal error Unsupported 9 The capability gate refuses the command BufferTooSmall to NotImplemented 16 to 38 Transport, session, object, policy and attestation errors; ToString names each ThroughputLimited 39 The chip answered SW 0x66A6: its APDU throughput limit Result carries .error and a .detail with the status word and the layer. The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. All buffers are fixed by Config limits and caller-supplied spans. A Device holds its command and response buffers and four secure-messaging pipes (platform SCP03, AESKey, ECKey, UserID) as members: about 11 KiB, so place it in static storage on a small target. The largest plain command is kMaxPlainCommandApdu (1033 bytes); the largest on the wire, with an applet session inside platform SCP03, is kMaxCommandApdu (1108 bytes). Contract amendments of the device package ¶ Device::SetPlatformKeys() (the platform key handles for Open() and Recover() ) and Device::ReadEckaPublicKey() (the attested ECKA key that BeginEcKeySession() requires). Execute() does not compile for the commands the device runs itself ( detail::IsDeviceOwned : the select, the session handshake steps, TriggerSelfTest ). AuthRole::Restrict (RESERVED_ID_RESTRICT, DisableObjCreation ). TlsPrfArgs::role ( TlsRole::Client or Server , AN12543 4.17.3). kMaxPlainCommandApdu , kSecureMessagingOverhead , kSessionFrameOverhead ; kMaxCommandApdu from 1024 to 1108. ReferenceCrypto::kSlots from 8 to 16 (two stacked secure-messaging layers hold eight keys). Contract amendments of the facade and the irreversible operations ¶ hrot : typed slots per kind ( Slot , DataSlot , CounterSlot , CertSlot , each with At() checked at compile time and Make() at run time; MakeSlot() kept); keys typed by use ( Key : SignKey , AttestKey , AgreeKey , TlsKey , VerifyKey ) replace KeyHandle ; Provision(slot) and Find(slot) (NIST P-256 only) replace Provision(slot, use, curve) ; GetPublicKey() returns EcPublicKey ; Sign() and TlsSign() return Signature ; VerifySignature() fails closed ( Result ) and replaces Verify() ; Agree() , ImportPublicKey() , TrustAttestationKey() , Attest(key, slot) for every slot kind, Store() , Load() , Erase() , the certificate calls, CreateCounter() , RaiseCounterTo() , SetWindowCount() , ApduBudget::Used() and Allows() ; CheckPlan() takes a span. Wrap() and Unwrap() are gone: the chip has no RFC 3394 wrap for the host, and a wrapped import is the device's WriteSymmKey with a key-encryption key. CheckFloor(floor, version) is Ok when the version is not below the counter. irreversible : every operation tag names its plan arguments ( Op::Args , NoArgs , ImmutableObjectArgs , FiniteAuthArgs ); Plan::Arguments() ; PlanCreateImmutableObject(id, policy, data) and PlanCreateFiniteAuthObject(id, policy, secret, max_attempts) take what the creating command needs. Device::ReadVerified() : an attested read and its verification in one call (the facade's attestation and ReadEckaPublicKey() use it). Contract amendments of the PKI layer ¶ Layer::Pki (value 9) is appended to Layer : a refusal of the optional PKI layer ( se05x_pki.hpp ) carries it, with the precise pki::Reason in Detail::step ( pki::ReasonOf() ). Nothing else changes; the layer is opt-in and no other header includes it. It keeps no state between calls and allocates nothing: every buffer is the caller's ( Certificates (PKI) ). Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF ports in examples/esp32 are an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

If you have a newer revision, compare its revision history with the topics above; a change to a pin, a register, a timing or a value the driver uses is a bug report for this repository. Where the driver deliberately goes beyond the datasheet, the Contract says so. The repository never contains the PDF itself: vendors own their documents. Download it from the vendor, and compare its SHA-256 with the one above to confirm you have the same file.

docs.text: The driver is written against the revision above. If you have a newer revision, compare its revision history with the topics above; a change to a pin, a register, a timing or a value the driver uses is a bug report for this repository. Where the driver deliberately goes beyond the datasheet, the Contract says so. The repository never contains the PDF itself: vendors own their documents. Download it from the vendor, and compare its SHA-256 with the one above to confirm you have the same file.
docs.title: When the datasheet and the driver differ

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own ports, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the root-of-trust jobs through the facade against the simulated chip of the tests ( tests/model/ ), then opens a bus with nothing on it. No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/se05x_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest se05x_host_example ). PSA crypto port ¶ examples/psa/se05x_psa_crypto.hpp is an optional, header-only crypto port over the PSA Crypto API (mbedTLS 3.x, the ESP-IDF mbedtls component): every key the driver hands over lives in PSA as a volatile key, the driver holds handles only. It is the production replacement for ReferenceCrypto (S-15) and the ESP32 facade example uses it. Nothing of mbedTLS is in this repository. With MbedTLS 3 installed, the host build checks it against known answers and runs the whole stack with it (platform SCP03, an AESKey session, provision, attest and sign against the chip model): cmake -S . -B build -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DSE05X_BUILD_PSA_EXAMPLE = ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH = <mbedtls prefix> cmake --build build --target se05x_psa_check && ctest --test-dir build -R se05x_psa_check CI does not build it (no MbedTLS in the CI image); it was built and run on a workstation with MbedTLS 3.6.4. ESP32 ¶ An ESP-IDF application that opens the chip on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the ports in esp32_se05x_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. docs.text: The first 15 minutes ¶ From nothing to a chip that signs, in four steps. Steps 1 and 2 need no hardware. The first 15 minutes Figure description and sources Four steps in order, each with its minutes. Run the host example takes minutes 0 to 3. Read what it did takes minutes 3 to 6. Wire the chip takes minutes 6 to 11. Flash the ESP32 example takes minutes 11 to 15. The first two steps need no hardware. Drawn from: docs/model/first-15-minutes.graph.yml . 0 to 3 minutes: run the host example ¶ The host example runs every facade job against the simulated chip of the tests: open with platform SCP03, identify, provision a key, attest it, sign, seal a configuration and check an anti-rollback floor. From the repository root: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/se05x_host_example The output, line for line (a CTest checks that this page shows what the example prints): SE05X driver 0.1.0 on the host, simulated chip Open with platform SCP03 Ok Identify Ok applet 7.2.0, OEF id A921 Provision a signing key in slot 0 Ok Provision slot 0 again ObjectExists Attest the key (verified) Ok Sign a digest Ok Verify the signature on the chip Ok Seal a configuration Ok Create the firmware floor at 3 Ok Boot image version 4 Ok Boot image version 2 (a rollback) PolicyDenied APDUs sent: 23 Close Ok Open with nothing on the bus Nack 3 to 6 minutes: read what it did ¶ ObjectExists on the second provision: a facade key slot is never overwritten ( Device identity ). PolicyDenied for version 2: the floor at 3 refuses a rollback ( Anti-rollback ). APDUs sent: 23 : the budget the SE052F's throughput limit needs (AN13904 p. 28). Nack with nothing on the bus: a missing chip is an error, never a hang. Choose your job maps every job the chip does to a guide. 6 to 11 minutes: wire the chip ¶ MCU SE050, SE051 (HX2QFN20) SE052 (HVQFN20) I2C SDA, pull-up SDA, pin 9 SDA, pin 11 I2C SCL, pull-up SCL, pin 10 SCL, pin 10 GPIO (reset port) ENA, pin 11 RST_N, pin 14 3.3 V VIN, pin 12; VOUT to VCC VIN, pin 12; VOUT to VDD GND VSS, pin 19 VSS, pin 19 Pins from SE050 Table 5 (p. 11), SE051 Table 3 (p. 12) and SE052 Table 2 (p. 4); both lines must be high at power-up (SE050 section 3.4, p. 8). The figures of each package are on Where to use it . 11 to 15 minutes: flash the ESP32 example ¶ With ESP-IDF v5.5, an ESP32-C6 and the chip wired to the default pins of Esp32Se05xPins (SDA GPIO6, SCL GPIO7, ENA GPIO11; on an SE052 set reset_n to the RST_N GPIO and enable to -1): cd examples/esp32 git submodule update --init scripts # the ESP-IDF build scripts . $IDF_PATH /export.sh # ESP-IDF v5.5 ./scripts/build_app.sh se05x_hrot_example Release ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor se05x_hrot_example Release The monitor shows the same jobs against the real chip. Without your platform keys the facade refuses key operations with PolicyDenied and says so: give your keys through the crypto port ( Secure channel ), never the vendor's default key set in a product. Bench step (not verified on hardware): run the ESP32 example on an SE050E and on an SE052F dev kit and compare the log with the host transcript above; the identity and the APDU count differ, every status should match.

docs.text: Getting started by job ¶ One short path for each thing people use a secure element for. Each path names the calls, the chip objects and policies they create, what can go wrong and where the chip documents it. Open the device first ( Quickstart ); every path below starts from an open se05x::Device and, for the facade, an se05x::hrot::Device bound to it. Datasheet sections this page relies on Reserved object identifiers: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Table 5, p. 10 Attestation: hash of the command, no freshness echo (applet 7.x): NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Attestation, p. 19 Session policy and object policy headers: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Tables 62 and 63, p. 66 Session commands: CreateSession to ECKeySessionInternalAuthenticate: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Session management commands, p. 68 WriteECKey and key generation on the chip: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteECKey, p. 80 WriteSymmKey, RFC 3394 wrapped import: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteSymmKey, p. 83 WriteBinary, WriteUserID, WriteCounter: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteBinary, WriteUserID, WriteCounter, p. 84 ImportExternalObject: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ImportExternalObject, p. 88 ReadObject and the attested read: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ReadObject, p. 89 ECDSASign and ECDSAVerify: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ECDSASign, ECDSAVerify, p. 101 ECDHGenerateSharedSecret: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ECDHGenerateSharedSecret, p. 105 GetVersion, GetTimestamp, GetFreeMemory, GetRandom: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Generic management commands, p. 151 Edwards and Montgomery byte order on the wire: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Edwards and Montgomery byte order, p. 168 Pre-provisioned attestation keys: NXP AN12436 Rev. 2.4, Tables 8 and 9, p. 10 Attestation formats 1 and 2: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, Attested read, p. 248 Timestamp layout: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, GetTimestamp, p. 253 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Every snippet on this page is compiled for the board ports of the Quickstart ( tests/docs/jobs.hpp ) and run against the chip model in the host tests ( tests/test_docs_jobs.cpp ). Secure messaging first Every facade key forbids use without secure messaging, and so do counters and secret data: over a bus that can be probed, an unauthenticated answer (a signature check, a counter value) could be forged, and a clear one read. Open the device with platform SCP03 (or an AESKey session) before these jobs. A call whose result you act on (keys, counters, verification) needs authenticated answers, an R-MAC layer ( CMacRMac or Full ); ECDH and Protection::Secret data need encryption both ways as well ( Full ). Otherwise the facade refuses with PolicyDenied (layer Hrot ) and sends nothing. Identity, random numbers, public data and certificates work without it. For a root of trust set ScpPolicy::Require : Auto decides from an unauthenticated answer ( Security model ). Job Facade call Page section Provision a key hrot::Device::Provision<U>() Provision Attest hrot::Device::Attest() Attest Sign and verify Sign() , VerifySignature() Sign and verify ECDH Agree() ECDH Key import ImportPublicKey() ; Device with WriteSymmKeyArgs Key import Secure channel Device::SetPlatformKeys() , Begin*Session() Secure channel Secure storage Store() , Load() Secure storage Certificates StoreCertificate() , LoadCertificate() Certificates Counters CheckFloor() , RaiseCounterTo() Counters Lifecycle and lock irreversible::Operations Lifecycle Open a secure channel ¶ Channel Call When Platform SCP03 Device::SetPlatformKeys() , then Open() with Config::scp_policy The bus can be probed; mandatory on SE050F and when the chip requires it AESKey session BeginAesKeySession() SCP03 at the applet, one AES authentication object ECKey session BeginEcKeySession() Bind one host key pair to the chip UserID session BeginUserIdSession() Application separation under a trusted host OS; no secure messaging Platform SCP03, with the keys as handles of your crypto port (never key bytes in the image, never a vendor default key set in a product): /// Open the chip with platform SCP03. The keys are handles in your crypto port: never compile key /// bytes into the image, and never use a vendor default key set in a product. template < PortSet P > Error OpenSecure ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , KeyRef platform_enc , KeyRef platform_mac ) noexcept { scp03 :: ChannelParams keys {}; keys . keys . enc = platform_enc ; keys . keys . mac = platform_mac ; if ( const auto given = device . SetPlatformKeys ( keys ); ! given . ok ()) { return given . error ; } return device . Open (). error ; // Config::scp_policy = ScpPolicy::Require when the device was built } An AESKey session over the default session: /// Open an AESKey session with an authentication object of the chip. `key` is a handle in your /// crypto port; the session ends with EndSession() or Close(). template < PortSet P > Error OpenAesKeySession ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , ObjectId credential , KeyRef key ) noexcept { AesKeySessionParams params {}; params . credential = credential ; params . keys . enc = key ; const auto opened = device . BeginAesKeySession ( params ); if ( opened . error == Error :: NeedsReselect ) { return device . Recover (). error ; // a lost frame under a session: recover, then open it again } return opened . error ; } EndSession() closes it. A failed step wipes the session keys; a session that failed after CreateSession cannot be closed, so the device selects the applet again (AN12543 3.6.5 p. 35). The ECKey session is off unless the build sets SE05X_ENABLE_ECKEY_SESSION=1 , and it needs the chip's ECKA key verified first ( Device::ReadEckaPublicKey ). A lost frame or a failed check under a session leaves the device NeedsReopen : call Device::Recover() , then open the session again. A UserID session alone is not secure messaging: the facade refuses key use over it. A facade policy names the default session (authentication object 0) and, when the facade runs inside an AESKey or ECKey session, that session's credential: id 0 does not cover other sessions (AN12543 3.7.1.2, p. 36), so an object made in one session is refused in another ( Ambiguities , A20). Diagrams and details: Secure channels . Provision a device key ¶ CheckPlan() sends nothing and says whether each slot's policy builds for this chip. Provision<U>(slot) generates a NIST P-256 key pair inside the chip (WriteECKey with no key bytes, AN12543 p. 80) under the strict policy of its use: the use's rule, read of the public half, secure messaging; write, delete and regenerate forbidden. A slot already in use gives ObjectExists and nothing is changed; Find<U>(slot) returns the key. /// Generate the device key in slot 0 and read its public half. template < PortSet P > Error ProvisionDeviceKey ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: EcPublicKey & public_key ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: Slot kDeviceKey = hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > (); const std :: array < hrot :: SlotPlan , 1 > plan { hrot :: SlotPlan { kDeviceKey , hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign }}; if ( const auto checked = hrot . CheckPlan ( plan ); ! checked . ok ()) { return checked . error ; // nothing was sent } const auto key = hrot . template Provision < hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign > ( kDeviceKey ); if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; // ObjectExists: the slot was provisioned before; use Find() } const auto pub = hrot . GetPublicKey ( key . value ); public_key = pub . value ; return pub . error ; } A facade key is permanent The strict policy forbids deleting the key, so the slot stays occupied for the life of the chip; only a factory reset ( Irreversible operations , DeleteAllObjects ) removes it. Plan the slots before you provision. The key never leaves the chip. A Key<U> ( SignKey , AttestKey , AgreeKey , TlsKey , VerifyKey ) names the slot only, only the facade makes a valid one, and each call takes only its own key type: Sign() with an AgreeKey does not compile. Attest a key or a value ¶ Attest(key, slot) returns Verified<AttestedValue> only when every check passed: a fresh 16-byte nonce from the host's crypto port for every request, never from the chip being attested (its answer could be replayed with an old attested answer); applet 3.x (format 1): the chip echoes the nonce and it must match; applet 7.x (format 2): the signature covers the hash of the command the chip received and the returned TLVs (AN12543 p. 19); a timestamp later than the last one accepted from this chip, across reopens (AN12543 3.9, p. 42), the signature with the attestation key you trust over the TLVs exactly as the chip returned them, and the 18-byte unique id equal to the one read in this open of the device (else Counterfeit ). /// Prove that the key in slot 0 lives in this chip. `vendor_public` must come from a verified /// certificate (the se05x::pki layer) or your factory record, never from the same chip. template < PortSet P > Error AttestDeviceKey ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & vendor_public , hrot :: EcPublicKey & attested_key ) noexcept { const auto trusted = hrot :: TrustAttestationKey ( FromReserved ( ReservedId :: RootOfTrustKey ), vendor_public ); if ( ! trusted . ok ()) { return trusted . error ; } const auto value = hrot . Attest ( trusted . value , hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > ()); if ( ! value . ok ()) { return value . error ; // AttestationInvalid, Counterfeit: do not trust this chip } const hrot :: AttestedValue & checked = value . value . Get (); // a Verified<T> exists only if checked if ( checked . data . length != attested_key . point . size ()) { return Error :: FrameError ; // not an uncompressed P-256 point } for ( std :: size_t i = 0U ; i < attested_key . point . size (); ++ i ) { attested_key . point [ i ] = checked . data . bytes [ i ]; } return Error :: Ok ; } The trusted public key decides what the attestation proves. For the vendor key ( 0xF0000012 , AN12436 p. 10) take it from the vendor certificate after its chain was verified (the optional se05x::pki layer ); reading it from the same chip proves nothing. A value that failed any check cannot become a Verified<T> : you get AttestationInvalid . The facade returns up to 256 bytes of attested data. Sign and verify ¶ Sign(key, digest) signs a SHA-256 digest you computed (ECDSA takes a digest, AN12543 p. 101) and returns the DER signature. VerifySignature() fails closed: Ok only for a valid signature, AttestationInvalid for one that does not verify, never a true / false to forget. /// Sign a SHA-256 digest with the device key and check the signature on the chip. template < PortSet P > Error SignAndVerify ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Digest digest , hrot :: Signature & out ) noexcept { const auto key = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > ()); if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; } const auto signature = hrot . Sign ( key . value , digest ); if ( ! signature . ok ()) { return signature . error ; // PolicyDenied: no secure messaging } out = signature . value ; return hrot . VerifySignature ( key . value , digest , out . View ()). error ; // Ok only when valid } Agree a key (ECDH) ¶ Agree(key, peer, shared) returns the 32-byte x coordinate of the shared point (ECDHGenerateSharedSecret, AN12543 p. 105) into a SecretBuffer that wipes itself. The secret crosses the bus encrypted only ( Full ). A chip whose extended features forbid ECDH ( EXTCFG_CRYPTO_EC_FORBID_ECDH ) gives Unsupported before anything is sent. /// Agree a secret with a peer. The key lives in slot 1; the secret is wiped when `shared` goes. template < PortSet P > Error AgreeWithPeer ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & peer , SecretBuffer < 32 >& shared ) noexcept { auto key = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Agree > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 1 > ()); if ( key . error == Error :: ObjectNotFound ) { key = hrot . template Provision < hrot :: KeyUse :: Agree > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 1 > ()); } if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; } return hrot . Agree ( key . value , peer , shared ). error ; } Import a key ¶ Generating keys inside the chip is the default. A trust anchor (a firmware-signing root, a server key) comes from outside: ImportPublicKey() stores it in a key slot where it can verify and never be changed or deleted. /// Keep the firmware-signing root in the chip: it verifies, and nobody can replace it. template < PortSet P > Error StoreFirmwareRoot ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & root ) noexcept { return hrot . ImportPublicKey ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 2 > (), root ). error ; } /// Verify a firmware image's signature with that root. template < PortSet P > Error CheckFirmware ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Digest image_digest , ByteSpan signature ) noexcept { const auto root = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Verify > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 2 > ()); if ( ! root . ok ()) { return root . error ; } return hrot . VerifySignature ( root . value , image_digest , signature ). error ; } A symmetric key travels wrapped (RFC 3394) under a key-encryption key already in the chip, so the plain key never exists on the host (WriteSymmKey, AN12543 p. 83). The facade has no symmetric keys; this is the device layer: /// Import an AES key wrapped (RFC 3394) under a key-encryption key already in the chip: the plain /// key never exists on the host. This is the device layer: the facade has no symmetric keys. template < PortSet P > Error ImportWrappedAesKey ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , ObjectId kek , ObjectId target , ByteSpan wrapped ) noexcept { const auto policy = PolicyBuilder < AppletGeneration :: V7 , ObjectClass :: AesKey , Profile :: Strict > {} . ForAllOthers () . template Allow < Rule :: Encrypt > () . template Allow < Rule :: Decrypt > () . RequireSecureMessaging () . template Forbid < Rule :: Write > () . template Forbid < Rule :: Delete > () . Build (); if ( ! policy . ok ()) { return policy . error ; } WriteSymmKeyArgs args {}; args . id = target ; args . policy = & policy . value ; args . type = SymmKeyType :: Aes ; args . key = wrapped ; // 24 or 40 bytes: an AES-128 or AES-256 key wrapped args . kek = kek ; return device . template Execute < Command :: WriteSymmKey > ( args ). error ; } A plain private key can be imported with WriteEcKeyArgs for provisioning only; it shows Origin::External in every attestation. ImportExternalObject (AN12543 p. 88) is held: the vendor asks to be contacted before use. Store data ¶ Store(slot, data, protection) creates a binary object of 1 to 2048 bytes (written 256 bytes per command); Protection::Secret needs secure messaging for every read, write and delete (AN12543 p. 84), over encrypted traffic. Load() reads the size from the chip, then the data. A slot in use gives ObjectExists : Erase() first. The object is one byte longer than the data: Store writes a completion marker after the last chunk and Load refuses an object without it ( FrameError ), so a store cut short by a power loss is never read back as a value; a store that fails while powered deletes the object (A35), except after SW 0x66A6 ( ThroughputLimited ), when the chip refuses work: then the object stays until Erase() . /// Keep a configuration blob that only a host with secure messaging reads back. template < PortSet P > Error SealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan config ) noexcept { return hrot . Store ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), config , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ). error ; } /// Read it back; the length comes from the chip. template < PortSet P > Result < std :: size_t > UnsealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { return hrot . Load ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), out , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ); } Read and store certificates ¶ A certificate slot holds the bytes as given: the facade parses nothing. The vendor provisions certificates of its own keys (AN12436 Tables 8 and 9, p. 10). Anyone on the bus may read a certificate, and also replace it: its integrity is its signature, so check it before you trust it. Building a CSR and parsing or verifying X.509 is the optional se05x::pki layer . /// Store the device certificate your CA issued, and read it back for the TLS stack. The bytes are /// not parsed here: building and checking X.509 is the se05x::pki layer. template < PortSet P > Error KeepCertificate ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan der , MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: CertSlot kDeviceCert = hrot :: CertSlot :: At < 0 > (); if ( const auto stored = hrot . StoreCertificate ( kDeviceCert , der ); ! stored . ok ()) { return stored . error ; // ObjectExists: EraseCertificate() first to replace it } return hrot . LoadCertificate ( kDeviceCert , out ). error ; } Monotonic counters ¶ A counter slot holds a 4-byte counter that only goes up (WriteCounter, AN12543 p. 84), created with its start value in one command. Its policy forbids delete, so a floor cannot be deleted and created again lower; only a factory reset removes it. CheckFloor(slot, version) fails closed: Ok only when version is not below the counter, PolicyDenied for an older one. RaiseCounterTo() moves the floor in one command, never down; a loop of CounterIncrement() would spend the APDU budget ( S-17 ). See the HRoT cookbook . /// The anti-rollback check at boot: refuse an image older than one that ran before. template < PortSet P > Error BootCheck ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: CounterSlot kFloor = hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (); return hrot . CheckFloor ( kFloor , image_version ). error ; // Ok only when not below the floor } /// After the new image booted and passed its self test: raise the floor in one command. template < PortSet P > Error CommitImage ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { return hrot . RaiseCounterTo ( hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (), image_version ). error ; } Lifecycle and lock ¶ Locking the transport, requiring platform SCP03, restricting object creation, changing applet features and the factory reset are lifecycle operations ( Lifecycle ). Those that cannot be undone exist only in a build with SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE=1 and go plan, confirm, apply ( Irreversible operations ): /// Lock the transport for good. Run it from a session with the Transport credential; show the /// plan's effect to a person; the phrase is typed by that person, not by the code that planned it. template < se05x :: PortSet P > se05x :: Error LockForGood ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , const se05x :: irreversible :: Phrase & typed , void ( * show )( const char * effect )) noexcept { using Op = se05x :: irreversible :: SetLockStatePersistent ; se05x :: irreversible :: Operations < P > operations ( device ); const auto plan = operations . PlanSetLockStatePersistent (); // sends nothing if ( ! plan . ok ()) { return plan . error ; // ConditionsNotSatisfied: not a Transport session; WrongState: locked } show ( plan . value . Effect ()); return operations . Apply ( plan . value , se05x :: irreversible :: Confirmation < Op > { typed }). error ; } Read the current state at any time with ReadState.

docs.text: One short path for each thing people use a secure element for. Each path names the calls, the chip objects and policies they create, what can go wrong and where the chip documents it. Open the device first ( Quickstart ); every path below starts from an open se05x::Device and, for the facade, an se05x::hrot::Device bound to it. Datasheet sections this page relies on Reserved object identifiers: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Table 5, p. 10 Attestation: hash of the command, no freshness echo (applet 7.x): NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Attestation, p. 19 Session policy and object policy headers: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Tables 62 and 63, p. 66 Session commands: CreateSession to ECKeySessionInternalAuthenticate: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Session management commands, p. 68 WriteECKey and key generation on the chip: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteECKey, p. 80 WriteSymmKey, RFC 3394 wrapped import: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteSymmKey, p. 83 WriteBinary, WriteUserID, WriteCounter: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, WriteBinary, WriteUserID, WriteCounter, p. 84 ImportExternalObject: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ImportExternalObject, p. 88 ReadObject and the attested read: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ReadObject, p. 89 ECDSASign and ECDSAVerify: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ECDSASign, ECDSAVerify, p. 101 ECDHGenerateSharedSecret: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ECDHGenerateSharedSecret, p. 105 GetVersion, GetTimestamp, GetFreeMemory, GetRandom: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Generic management commands, p. 151 Edwards and Montgomery byte order on the wire: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Edwards and Montgomery byte order, p. 168 Pre-provisioned attestation keys: NXP AN12436 Rev. 2.4, Tables 8 and 9, p. 10 Attestation formats 1 and 2: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, Attested read, p. 248 Timestamp layout: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, GetTimestamp, p. 253 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Every snippet on this page is compiled for the board ports of the Quickstart ( tests/docs/jobs.hpp ) and run against the chip model in the host tests ( tests/test_docs_jobs.cpp ). Secure messaging first Every facade key forbids use without secure messaging, and so do counters and secret data: over a bus that can be probed, an unauthenticated answer (a signature check, a counter value) could be forged, and a clear one read. Open the device with platform SCP03 (or an AESKey session) before these jobs. A call whose result you act on (keys, counters, verification) needs authenticated answers, an R-MAC layer ( CMacRMac or Full ); ECDH and Protection::Secret data need encryption both ways as well ( Full ). Otherwise the facade refuses with PolicyDenied (layer Hrot ) and sends nothing. Identity, random numbers, public data and certificates work without it. For a root of trust set ScpPolicy::Require : Auto decides from an unauthenticated answer ( Security model ). Job Facade call Page section Provision a key hrot::Device::Provision<U>() Provision Attest hrot::Device::Attest() Attest Sign and verify Sign() , VerifySignature() Sign and verify ECDH Agree() ECDH Key import ImportPublicKey() ; Device with WriteSymmKeyArgs Key import Secure channel Device::SetPlatformKeys() , Begin*Session() Secure channel Secure storage Store() , Load() Secure storage Certificates StoreCertificate() , LoadCertificate() Certificates Counters CheckFloor() , RaiseCounterTo() Counters Lifecycle and lock irreversible::Operations Lifecycle

docs.text: Channel Call When Platform SCP03 Device::SetPlatformKeys() , then Open() with Config::scp_policy The bus can be probed; mandatory on SE050F and when the chip requires it AESKey session BeginAesKeySession() SCP03 at the applet, one AES authentication object ECKey session BeginEcKeySession() Bind one host key pair to the chip UserID session BeginUserIdSession() Application separation under a trusted host OS; no secure messaging Platform SCP03, with the keys as handles of your crypto port (never key bytes in the image, never a vendor default key set in a product): /// Open the chip with platform SCP03. The keys are handles in your crypto port: never compile key /// bytes into the image, and never use a vendor default key set in a product. template < PortSet P > Error OpenSecure ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , KeyRef platform_enc , KeyRef platform_mac ) noexcept { scp03 :: ChannelParams keys {}; keys . keys . enc = platform_enc ; keys . keys . mac = platform_mac ; if ( const auto given = device . SetPlatformKeys ( keys ); ! given . ok ()) { return given . error ; } return device . Open (). error ; // Config::scp_policy = ScpPolicy::Require when the device was built } An AESKey session over the default session: /// Open an AESKey session with an authentication object of the chip. `key` is a handle in your /// crypto port; the session ends with EndSession() or Close(). template < PortSet P > Error OpenAesKeySession ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , ObjectId credential , KeyRef key ) noexcept { AesKeySessionParams params {}; params . credential = credential ; params . keys . enc = key ; const auto opened = device . BeginAesKeySession ( params ); if ( opened . error == Error :: NeedsReselect ) { return device . Recover (). error ; // a lost frame under a session: recover, then open it again } return opened . error ; } EndSession() closes it. A failed step wipes the session keys; a session that failed after CreateSession cannot be closed, so the device selects the applet again (AN12543 3.6.5 p. 35). The ECKey session is off unless the build sets SE05X_ENABLE_ECKEY_SESSION=1 , and it needs the chip's ECKA key verified first ( Device::ReadEckaPublicKey ). A lost frame or a failed check under a session leaves the device NeedsReopen : call Device::Recover() , then open the session again. A UserID session alone is not secure messaging: the facade refuses key use over it. A facade policy names the default session (authentication object 0) and, when the facade runs inside an AESKey or ECKey session, that session's credential: id 0 does not cover other sessions (AN12543 3.7.1.2, p. 36), so an object made in one session is refused in another ( Ambiguities , A20). Diagrams and details: Secure channels .
docs.title: Open a secure channel

docs.text: CheckPlan() sends nothing and says whether each slot's policy builds for this chip. Provision<U>(slot) generates a NIST P-256 key pair inside the chip (WriteECKey with no key bytes, AN12543 p. 80) under the strict policy of its use: the use's rule, read of the public half, secure messaging; write, delete and regenerate forbidden. A slot already in use gives ObjectExists and nothing is changed; Find<U>(slot) returns the key. /// Generate the device key in slot 0 and read its public half. template < PortSet P > Error ProvisionDeviceKey ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: EcPublicKey & public_key ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: Slot kDeviceKey = hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > (); const std :: array < hrot :: SlotPlan , 1 > plan { hrot :: SlotPlan { kDeviceKey , hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign }}; if ( const auto checked = hrot . CheckPlan ( plan ); ! checked . ok ()) { return checked . error ; // nothing was sent } const auto key = hrot . template Provision < hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign > ( kDeviceKey ); if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; // ObjectExists: the slot was provisioned before; use Find() } const auto pub = hrot . GetPublicKey ( key . value ); public_key = pub . value ; return pub . error ; } A facade key is permanent The strict policy forbids deleting the key, so the slot stays occupied for the life of the chip; only a factory reset ( Irreversible operations , DeleteAllObjects ) removes it. Plan the slots before you provision. The key never leaves the chip. A Key<U> ( SignKey , AttestKey , AgreeKey , TlsKey , VerifyKey ) names the slot only, only the facade makes a valid one, and each call takes only its own key type: Sign() with an AgreeKey does not compile.
docs.title: Provision a device key

docs.text: Attest(key, slot) returns Verified<AttestedValue> only when every check passed: a fresh 16-byte nonce from the host's crypto port for every request, never from the chip being attested (its answer could be replayed with an old attested answer); applet 3.x (format 1): the chip echoes the nonce and it must match; applet 7.x (format 2): the signature covers the hash of the command the chip received and the returned TLVs (AN12543 p. 19); a timestamp later than the last one accepted from this chip, across reopens (AN12543 3.9, p. 42), the signature with the attestation key you trust over the TLVs exactly as the chip returned them, and the 18-byte unique id equal to the one read in this open of the device (else Counterfeit ). /// Prove that the key in slot 0 lives in this chip. `vendor_public` must come from a verified /// certificate (the se05x::pki layer) or your factory record, never from the same chip. template < PortSet P > Error AttestDeviceKey ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & vendor_public , hrot :: EcPublicKey & attested_key ) noexcept { const auto trusted = hrot :: TrustAttestationKey ( FromReserved ( ReservedId :: RootOfTrustKey ), vendor_public ); if ( ! trusted . ok ()) { return trusted . error ; } const auto value = hrot . Attest ( trusted . value , hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > ()); if ( ! value . ok ()) { return value . error ; // AttestationInvalid, Counterfeit: do not trust this chip } const hrot :: AttestedValue & checked = value . value . Get (); // a Verified<T> exists only if checked if ( checked . data . length != attested_key . point . size ()) { return Error :: FrameError ; // not an uncompressed P-256 point } for ( std :: size_t i = 0U ; i < attested_key . point . size (); ++ i ) { attested_key . point [ i ] = checked . data . bytes [ i ]; } return Error :: Ok ; } The trusted public key decides what the attestation proves. For the vendor key ( 0xF0000012 , AN12436 p. 10) take it from the vendor certificate after its chain was verified (the optional se05x::pki layer ); reading it from the same chip proves nothing. A value that failed any check cannot become a Verified<T> : you get AttestationInvalid . The facade returns up to 256 bytes of attested data.
docs.title: Attest a key or a value

docs.text: Sign(key, digest) signs a SHA-256 digest you computed (ECDSA takes a digest, AN12543 p. 101) and returns the DER signature. VerifySignature() fails closed: Ok only for a valid signature, AttestationInvalid for one that does not verify, never a true / false to forget. /// Sign a SHA-256 digest with the device key and check the signature on the chip. template < PortSet P > Error SignAndVerify ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Digest digest , hrot :: Signature & out ) noexcept { const auto key = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Sign > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 0 > ()); if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; } const auto signature = hrot . Sign ( key . value , digest ); if ( ! signature . ok ()) { return signature . error ; // PolicyDenied: no secure messaging } out = signature . value ; return hrot . VerifySignature ( key . value , digest , out . View ()). error ; // Ok only when valid }
docs.title: Sign and verify

docs.text: Agree(key, peer, shared) returns the 32-byte x coordinate of the shared point (ECDHGenerateSharedSecret, AN12543 p. 105) into a SecretBuffer that wipes itself. The secret crosses the bus encrypted only ( Full ). A chip whose extended features forbid ECDH ( EXTCFG_CRYPTO_EC_FORBID_ECDH ) gives Unsupported before anything is sent. /// Agree a secret with a peer. The key lives in slot 1; the secret is wiped when `shared` goes. template < PortSet P > Error AgreeWithPeer ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & peer , SecretBuffer < 32 >& shared ) noexcept { auto key = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Agree > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 1 > ()); if ( key . error == Error :: ObjectNotFound ) { key = hrot . template Provision < hrot :: KeyUse :: Agree > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 1 > ()); } if ( ! key . ok ()) { return key . error ; } return hrot . Agree ( key . value , peer , shared ). error ; }
docs.title: Agree a key (ECDH)

docs.text: Generating keys inside the chip is the default. A trust anchor (a firmware-signing root, a server key) comes from outside: ImportPublicKey() stores it in a key slot where it can verify and never be changed or deleted. /// Keep the firmware-signing root in the chip: it verifies, and nobody can replace it. template < PortSet P > Error StoreFirmwareRoot ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: EcPublicKey & root ) noexcept { return hrot . ImportPublicKey ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 2 > (), root ). error ; } /// Verify a firmware image's signature with that root. template < PortSet P > Error CheckFirmware ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Digest image_digest , ByteSpan signature ) noexcept { const auto root = hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: Verify > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 2 > ()); if ( ! root . ok ()) { return root . error ; } return hrot . VerifySignature ( root . value , image_digest , signature ). error ; } A symmetric key travels wrapped (RFC 3394) under a key-encryption key already in the chip, so the plain key never exists on the host (WriteSymmKey, AN12543 p. 83). The facade has no symmetric keys; this is the device layer: /// Import an AES key wrapped (RFC 3394) under a key-encryption key already in the chip: the plain /// key never exists on the host. This is the device layer: the facade has no symmetric keys. template < PortSet P > Error ImportWrappedAesKey ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , ObjectId kek , ObjectId target , ByteSpan wrapped ) noexcept { const auto policy = PolicyBuilder < AppletGeneration :: V7 , ObjectClass :: AesKey , Profile :: Strict > {} . ForAllOthers () . template Allow < Rule :: Encrypt > () . template Allow < Rule :: Decrypt > () . RequireSecureMessaging () . template Forbid < Rule :: Write > () . template Forbid < Rule :: Delete > () . Build (); if ( ! policy . ok ()) { return policy . error ; } WriteSymmKeyArgs args {}; args . id = target ; args . policy = & policy . value ; args . type = SymmKeyType :: Aes ; args . key = wrapped ; // 24 or 40 bytes: an AES-128 or AES-256 key wrapped args . kek = kek ; return device . template Execute < Command :: WriteSymmKey > ( args ). error ; } A plain private key can be imported with WriteEcKeyArgs for provisioning only; it shows Origin::External in every attestation. ImportExternalObject (AN12543 p. 88) is held: the vendor asks to be contacted before use.
docs.title: Import a key

docs.text: Store(slot, data, protection) creates a binary object of 1 to 2048 bytes (written 256 bytes per command); Protection::Secret needs secure messaging for every read, write and delete (AN12543 p. 84), over encrypted traffic. Load() reads the size from the chip, then the data. A slot in use gives ObjectExists : Erase() first. The object is one byte longer than the data: Store writes a completion marker after the last chunk and Load refuses an object without it ( FrameError ), so a store cut short by a power loss is never read back as a value; a store that fails while powered deletes the object (A35), except after SW 0x66A6 ( ThroughputLimited ), when the chip refuses work: then the object stays until Erase() . /// Keep a configuration blob that only a host with secure messaging reads back. template < PortSet P > Error SealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan config ) noexcept { return hrot . Store ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), config , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ). error ; } /// Read it back; the length comes from the chip. template < PortSet P > Result < std :: size_t > UnsealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { return hrot . Load ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), out , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ); }
docs.title: Store data

docs.text: A certificate slot holds the bytes as given: the facade parses nothing. The vendor provisions certificates of its own keys (AN12436 Tables 8 and 9, p. 10). Anyone on the bus may read a certificate, and also replace it: its integrity is its signature, so check it before you trust it. Building a CSR and parsing or verifying X.509 is the optional se05x::pki layer . /// Store the device certificate your CA issued, and read it back for the TLS stack. The bytes are /// not parsed here: building and checking X.509 is the se05x::pki layer. template < PortSet P > Error KeepCertificate ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan der , MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: CertSlot kDeviceCert = hrot :: CertSlot :: At < 0 > (); if ( const auto stored = hrot . StoreCertificate ( kDeviceCert , der ); ! stored . ok ()) { return stored . error ; // ObjectExists: EraseCertificate() first to replace it } return hrot . LoadCertificate ( kDeviceCert , out ). error ; }
docs.title: Read and store certificates

docs.text: A counter slot holds a 4-byte counter that only goes up (WriteCounter, AN12543 p. 84), created with its start value in one command. Its policy forbids delete, so a floor cannot be deleted and created again lower; only a factory reset removes it. CheckFloor(slot, version) fails closed: Ok only when version is not below the counter, PolicyDenied for an older one. RaiseCounterTo() moves the floor in one command, never down; a loop of CounterIncrement() would spend the APDU budget ( S-17 ). See the HRoT cookbook . /// The anti-rollback check at boot: refuse an image older than one that ran before. template < PortSet P > Error BootCheck ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: CounterSlot kFloor = hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (); return hrot . CheckFloor ( kFloor , image_version ). error ; // Ok only when not below the floor } /// After the new image booted and passed its self test: raise the floor in one command. template < PortSet P > Error CommitImage ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { return hrot . RaiseCounterTo ( hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (), image_version ). error ; }

docs.text: Locking the transport, requiring platform SCP03, restricting object creation, changing applet features and the factory reset are lifecycle operations ( Lifecycle ). Those that cannot be undone exist only in a build with SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE=1 and go plan, confirm, apply ( Irreversible operations ): /// Lock the transport for good. Run it from a session with the Transport credential; show the /// plan's effect to a person; the phrase is typed by that person, not by the code that planned it. template < se05x :: PortSet P > se05x :: Error LockForGood ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , const se05x :: irreversible :: Phrase & typed , void ( * show )( const char * effect )) noexcept { using Op = se05x :: irreversible :: SetLockStatePersistent ; se05x :: irreversible :: Operations < P > operations ( device ); const auto plan = operations . PlanSetLockStatePersistent (); // sends nothing if ( ! plan . ok ()) { return plan . error ; // ConditionsNotSatisfied: not a Transport session; WrongState: locked } show ( plan . value . Effect ()); return operations . Apply ( plan . value , se05x :: irreversible :: Confirmation < Op > { typed }). error ; } Read the current state at any time with ReadState.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The SE050, SE051 and SE052 pins, bus settings, timing and power, as the driver uses them. The per-chip guides add the wiring and what differs: SE050 , SE051 , SE052 . Datasheet sections this page relies on Start-up: the interface is chosen by the line levels at boot: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 3.4 Startup behavior, p. 8 I2C target address 0x48: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 4.1 I2C interfaces, Figure 3, p. 8 I2C clock and clock stretching per variant: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 4.1.1 Supported I2C frequencies, p. 9 RST_N has no effect when only I2C is enabled: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 4.2 ISO7816 and ISO14443 interface, p. 9 Power-down and deep power-down modes: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 5 Power-saving modes, p. 9 Deep power-down supply: VIN, VOUT to VCC: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 5.2 Deep Power-down mode, p. 10 Pin table of the HX2QFN20 package (SE050): NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, Table 5 Pin description, p. 11 Supply range and pin reference voltages: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, Table 9 Recommended operating conditions, p. 13 ENA low time and glitches: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, Table 14 AC characteristics, p. 18 Pin table (SE051): NXP SE051 Rev. 2.0, Table 3 Pin description, p. 12 Pin table of the HVQFN20 package (SE052): NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, Table 2 Pin description, p. 4 SE052 supplies: VDD 1.62 V to 5.5 V, VIN 1.65 V to 3.6 V: NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, Table 13 IC supply current, p. 18 Development kit jumpers: ENA, reset, pull-ups: NXP AN13539 Rev. 1.2, Table 9 and the jumper tables, p. 15 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Packages ¶ Chips Package Size Control pins SE050, SE051 HX2QFN20 3 x 3 x 0.32 mm, 0.4 mm pitch ENA (deep power-down); RST_N is the ISO 7816 reset SE052 HVQFN20 4 x 4 x 0.85 mm, 0.5 mm pitch RST_N (device reset); no ENA; VDD in place of VCC The outline code of the SE052 is SOT917-7 in the data sheet and SOT917-6 in AN14028 (ambiguity A2). The HX2QFN20 figures below are drawn from docs/hardware.yml and show the SE050 and SE051, though their titles name the family; the SE052 has its own on SE052 . SE05x pinout, HX2QFN20 Figure description and sources The SE05x seen from the top, in its HX2QFN20 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . SE05x package, HX2QFN20 Figure description and sources The SE05x package seen from the top and, when the height is known, from the side, drawn to scale: 3.0 x 3.0 x 0.32 mm. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side at the stated pitch; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/se05x_ports.hpp . Pins (HX2QFN20) ¶ HX2QFN20, 20 pins and an exposed pad (Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11). referenced to VCC - Leave open (recommended) or tie to VCC Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 4 NC4 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 5 NC5 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 6 NC6 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 7 NC7 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 8 NC8 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 9 SDA bus (VIN) I2C target data, open drain, T=1 frames at address 0x48; needs a pull-up; referenced to VIN Write() / Read() Leave open Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 10 SCL bus (VIN) I2C target clock, open drain; needs a pull-up; referenced to VIN Write() / Read() Leave open Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 11 ENA digital in (VIN) Deep power-down enable: low enters deep power-down (no state retention), high leaves it and the chip boots; tENalt 2 us typical, no minimum printed (the ESP-IDF port holds 10 us); glitches below 0.4 V longer than 30 ns count SetEnable() / PowerCycle() Tie to VCC Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 12 VIN power (VIN) Supply of the I2C pads and the ISO 7816/14443 interfaces, and the logic supply when deep power-down is used; 1.62 V to 3.6 V - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 13 CLK digital in (VCC) ISO 7816 clock input; not used by this driver - Leave open (recommended) or tie to VCC Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, p. 11 14 RST_N digital in (VCC) ISO 7816 reset, active low; has no effect when only the I2C interface is enabled (section 4.2), so the driver does not use it - Tie to VCC or VSS Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 15 VOUT power output (VIN) Switched supply output; connect to VCC on the board when deep power-down is used (up to 25 mA, switch at most 1.1 ohm, Table 14) - Leave open Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 16 IO2 1 digital in/out (VOUT) ISO 7816 IO2, or SCL of the chip's own I2C controller (I2CM commands) - Leave open (recommended) or tie to VOUT Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 17 LA analog (VCC) ISO 14443 antenna connection; not used by this driver - Tie to VSS Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 18 VCC power (VCC) Logic and ISO 7816/14443 interface supply; connect to VOUT on the board when deep power-down is used, else to the supply - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 19 VSS ground Ground - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 20 NC20 not connected (GND) Not connected - - Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 EP VSS_EP ground Centre pad: not connected inside; connecting it to ground is recommended for thermal reasons - Tie to GND Table 5 Pin description HX2QFN20, continued, p. 12 Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . Two facts the pin table makes easy to miss: RST_N does not reset an I2C-only chip. It is the ISO 7816 reset and "has no effect" when only I2C is enabled (SE050 section 4.2, p. 9; SE051 p. 10). The driver's power cycle uses ENA, with VOUT wired to VCC. The interface is chosen at boot. The chip takes I2C only when SDA and SCL are both high at power-up (SE050 section 3.4, p. 8), and changes interface only after a reset. docs.text: HRoT cookbook ¶ Recipes that combine the jobs of Getting started by job into what a product needs from a hardware root of trust. Each recipe lists the chip objects it uses, the order of the calls and the checks that make it safe. They use the facade only, so every key gets the strict policy. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5: Attestation: hash of the command, no freshness echo (applet 7.x): Attestation, p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Every recipe's code is compiled ( tests/docs/jobs.hpp ) and run against the chip model in the host tests. The recipes assume the device is open with platform SCP03 (see Open a secure channel ). Device identity at the factory ¶ Identify() : the 18-byte unique id, the family, the applet version and the OEF id. Record them. CheckPlan() and Provision<KeyUse::Sign>() the device key in slot 0; GetPublicKey() reads the public half. Attest() the key with the vendor attestation key: the record now proves the key was born in this chip. Send the public key and the attestation to your certificate authority; store the certificate it returns with StoreCertificate() . /// The factory record: the chip identity and the device public key. template < PortSet P > Error FactoryRecord ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Identity & identity , hrot :: EcPublicKey & public_key ) noexcept { const auto id = hrot . Identify (); if ( ! id . ok ()) { return id . error ; } identity = id . value ; return ProvisionDeviceKey ( hrot , public_key ); // then attest it and send both to your CA } Never generate the key on the host and import it: an external key shows Origin::External in every attestation for the life of the chip. Building the CSR for step 4 is the optional se05x::pki layer . TLS client key ¶ A TlsKey signs the handshake digest with TlsSign() ; your TLS stack calls it from its private-key callback. The driver provides the signing call, not a TLS stack binding: wire this function into your stack's external-key hook. The certificate comes from LoadCertificate() . /// At start-up, once: find the TLS client key (three APDUs), and keep the handle. template < PortSet P > Result < hrot :: TlsKey > FindTlsKey ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot ) noexcept { return hrot . template Find < hrot :: KeyUse :: TlsClient > ( hrot :: Slot :: At < 3 > ()); } /// The private-key callback of a TLS stack: sign the handshake digest with the kept key, one /// APDU per handshake. template < PortSet P > Error TlsSignCallback ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , const hrot :: TlsKey & key , hrot :: Digest handshake_digest , hrot :: Signature & out ) noexcept { const auto signature = hrot . TlsSign ( key , handshake_digest ); out = signature . value ; return signature . error ; } For the host-side crypto of the driver itself (SCP03, the attestation check), the optional PSA crypto port in examples/psa/ replaces ReferenceCrypto with mbedTLS or any PSA Crypto implementation; the ESP32 example uses it. Anti-rollback floor for firmware ¶ Create a counter per image type with CreateCounter(slot, first_version) . At boot, after the image's signature checked out ( VerifySignature() with the firmware root of Key import ), CheckFloor(slot, image_version) : PolicyDenied means the image is older than one that ran before; refuse it. After the new image has booted and passed its self test, raise the floor with RaiseCounterTo() in one command. /// The anti-rollback check at boot: refuse an image older than one that ran before. template < PortSet P > Error BootCheck ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { constexpr hrot :: CounterSlot kFloor = hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (); return hrot . CheckFloor ( kFloor , image_version ). error ; // Ok only when not below the floor } /// After the new image booted and passed its self test: raise the floor in one command. template < PortSet P > Error CommitImage ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t image_version ) noexcept { return hrot . RaiseCounterTo ( hrot :: CounterSlot :: At < 0 > (), image_version ). error ; } A counter only goes up, and its policy forbids delete, so a rollback cannot lower the floor even with full control of the host: it can neither count down nor delete the counter and create it again lower. CreateCounter() sets the start value in the same command that creates the counter, so a lost power cannot leave a floor of 0; when the slot already holds a lower counter it is raised to the value asked. Authenticated answers (an R-MAC layer) keep a host on the bus from forging the value it reads. Sealed configuration ¶ Store a configuration blob as Protection::Secret : every read, write and delete needs secure messaging, and the facade sends it only over encrypted traffic ( Full ), so only a host that can open platform SCP03 (or a session) reads it, and nothing on the bus does. /// Keep a configuration blob that only a host with secure messaging reads back. template < PortSet P > Error SealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan config ) noexcept { return hrot . Store ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), config , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ). error ; } /// Read it back; the length comes from the chip. template < PortSet P > Result < std :: size_t > UnsealConfig ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , MutableByteSpan out ) noexcept { return hrot . Load ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 0 > (), out , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ); } To tie the read to a measured boot state as well, build the policy yourself with RequirePcr() and write it with Device::WriteBinary() ; the facade's policies have no PCR condition. Binding a host to the chip ¶ Open an ECKey session with the host's key pair: the chip holds the host's public key as an authentication object, so a chip moved to another board refuses that board. Verify the receipt ( Config::verify_eckey_receipt , on by default). The ECKey session is built only with SE05X_ENABLE_ECKEY_SESSION=1 . See Secure channels . Random numbers ¶ Random() reads the chip's DRG.4 generator (seeded by a PTG.2 TRNG, SE050 data sheet section 3.1.1), up to 1024 bytes per call. Without secure messaging the bytes are not authenticated: a host on the bus could replace them. /// A nonce from the chip's random number generator. template < PortSet P > Error Nonce ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , std :: array < uint8_t , 16 >& nonce ) noexcept { return hrot . Random ( MutableByteSpan { nonce }). error ; } Staying under the throughput limit ¶ Status word 0x66A6 stops the chip until a reset: more than one million APDUs within 34 days on the SE052F (AN13904 p. 28), possibly on the SE051. A host that polls once per second sends about 2.9 million APDUs in 34 days. The facade counts every APDU the device sends, across every Open() and recovery of the device object (the count saturates, it never wraps), and refuses a call whose worst-case APDU count would pass the ceiling with ThroughputLimited (layer Hrot , nothing sent, no reset). The count knows nothing of earlier boots of the host: persist it and give it back at boot with SetWindowCount() . Calls made through se05x::Device directly are counted but not admitted. Every facade call is admitted only when its worst case fits: the table below is hrot::cost , the number of APDUs a call may send at most, whatever path it takes, as long as the chip answers it (the CTest se05x_docs_costs checks that this table and the header agree, and edge tests check that no path passes its cost). One path goes past it: when the chip answers SW 0x66A6 anyway (its own count differs from yours, for example after a lost window count), the device resets the chip and selects the applet again, which sends up to four more APDUs (the select, the lifecycle read and, with platform SCP03, the two handshake commands), and the call returns ThroughputLimited without sending anything else ( Store then leaves its unfinished object for Erase instead of deleting it). Those APDUs are counted in Used() , so the count can end at most four past the ceiling; a test pins that bound. Constant APDUs Call kIdentify 1 Identify kProvision 2 Provision kFind 3 Find kGetPublicKey 1 GetPublicKey kImportPublicKey 2 ImportPublicKey kSign 1 Sign , TlsSign kVerifySignature 1 VerifySignature kAgree 1 Agree kAttest 2 Attest (1 once the unique id was read in this open) kStoreBase 3 Store , StoreCertificate , plus one per 256 bytes of data kLoadBase 2 Load , LoadCertificate , plus one per 256 bytes of the buffer, at most 2048 kErase 1 Erase , EraseCertificate kCreateCounter 5 CreateCounter (2 for a new counter) kCounterValue 1 CounterValue , CheckFloor kCounterIncrement 2 CounterIncrement kRaiseCounterTo 1 RaiseCounterTo kRandomPer512 1 Random , per 512 bytes /// At boot, give the facade the APDU count your application persisted for the last 34 days; it /// refuses a call that would pass the chip's ceiling (ThroughputLimited, nothing sent). template < PortSet P > uint32_t ApdusLeft ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , uint32_t persisted_count ) noexcept { hrot . SetWindowCount ( persisted_count ); const hrot :: ApduBudget budget = hrot . Budget (); if ( ! budget . applies ) { return budget . limit ; } return ( budget . Used () < budget . limit ) ? ( budget . limit - budget . Used ()) : 0U ; } Cache what does not change (the identity, the public keys, the certificates) and never poll the chip for time or randomness in a tight loop.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( se05x_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-se05x.git external/driver-se05x git submodule update --init external/driver-se05x Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-se05x ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE se05x::se05x ) se05x::se05x is an alias of the se05x INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect SE05X_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver SE05X_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-se05x -B build-se05x cmake --install build-se05x --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( se05x 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE se05x::se05x ) The target is se05x::se05x in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated se05x_version.h go to include/se05x/inc/ , the template implementation to include/se05x/src/se05x.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-se05x) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-se05x (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-se05x.git components/se05x se05x (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml se05x (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : se05x : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-se05x.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES se05x (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/se05x_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into se05x_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = se05x :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-se05x) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-se05x (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-se05x.git components/se05x se05x (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml se05x (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : se05x : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-se05x.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES se05x (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then.
