docs.text: Secure channels ¶ Four ways to talk to the IoT applet, from no protection to full encryption. Which to use is a question of who can reach the bus ( Security model ). Datasheet sections this page relies on JOS.1 wrong EC key length resets the chip, JOS.2 SCP03 counter: NXP SE050_Erratasheet Rev. 1.0, 3.12, 3.13, p. 11 ECKey session: master key, session keys, receipt: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, ECKey session, p. 22 Session commands: CreateSession to ECKeySessionInternalAuthenticate: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Session management commands, p. 68 Platform SCP03 with AES-128 and AES-256; keys in plain files are insecure: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, Platform SCP03, p. 152 ECKey session flow and receipt: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, ECKey session, p. 156 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Channel Authenticates Protects the bus Keys on the host Layer None (default session) nobody no none Device UserID session a 4 to 16 byte value no secure messaging the UserID Device::BeginUserIdSession() Platform SCP03 the host to the card manager C-MAC, C-ENC, R-MAC, R-ENC static ENC, MAC, DEK as KeyRef scp03::Channel AESKey session the host to an AES authentication object SCP03 at the applet one AES key as KeyRef Device::BeginAesKeySession() ECKey session the host's key pair to an EC authentication object yes, with a receipt host private key and an ephemeral key in the crypto port eckey::Session At most two applet sessions are open at once, besides the default session (AN12543 p. 50). One authentication object cannot open two sessions. Platform SCP03 ¶ Platform SCP03: opening the channel Figure description and sources Three parties, left to right: the driver's scp03 layer, the crypto port that holds the static platform keys as handles, and the chip's card manager. The driver sends INITIALIZE UPDATE with a host challenge; the chip answers with its challenge and card cryptogram. The crypto port derives the session keys from the static keys (the driver never sees them) and the driver checks the card cryptogram in constant time. EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE carries the host cryptogram and the security level; when platform SCP is required the level must be full C-MAC, C-ENC, R-MAC and R-ENC (AN12543 SetPlatformSCPRequest, p. 75). Every later APDU is wrapped (C-MAC, C-ENC) and every reply checked (R-MAC, R-ENC); a failed check closes the channel and wipes the keys. The normative SCP03 text is the GlobalPlatform SCP03 amendment, which is not in this driver's source set: the byte detail follows AN12543 p. 72 and the middleware oracle. Drawn from: inc/se05x_scp03.hpp SecurityLevel ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/scp03-session.py . Platform SCP03 runs on the card manager underneath the applet, with AES-128 or AES-256 keys (AN13030 p. 152). The driver never holds the static keys as bytes: your crypto port resolves a KeyRef and does the CMAC and CBC itself, so the keys can sit in a hardware key store. Config::scp_policy decides when it is opened; when the chip requires it (SetPlatformSCPRequest) every command must carry the full security level. The vendor publishes default platform keys for each configuration. They are not in this repository, and a product must replace them before it leaves the factory; keys kept in a plain file are insecure (AN13030 p. 152). The driver cannot replace them yet: PUT KEY needs the new keys encrypted under the DEK, which the crypto port cannot do without exposing them, so gp::CardManager::PutKeys (the ReplacePlatformKeys irreversible operation ) returns Unsupported and sends nothing, even with a valid confirmation. ECKey session ¶ ECKey session: opening it Figure description and sources The driver's eckey layer, the crypto port and the IoT applet. The driver first reads the chip's ECKA public key with an attested ReadObject and verifies the attestation. The crypto port makes a fresh ephemeral P-256 key pair for this session only and signs the request with the host's long-term key, whose public half is the ECKey authentication object on the chip. ECKeySessionInternalAuthenticate (84 88) carries the parameters (tag A6), the ephemeral public key (tag 7F49) and the signature (tag 5F37). The chip answers a 16-byte challenge and a 16-byte receipt. The host computes the shared secret, derives the master key (the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over a counter, the secret, the chip's random and the parameters) and the session keys by CMAC, and checks the receipt in constant time before it trusts the session. The ephemeral private key and the master key are wiped. AN12543 pp. 22-23, 33-34, 72-73; no vector confirms the derivation yet, so it is built behind a flag. Drawn from: inc/se05x_eckey.hpp ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/eckey-session.py . The ECKey session binds a host key pair to the chip: the chip holds the host's public key as an authentication object, and every session uses a fresh ephemeral key, made and wiped in the crypto port. The chip's receipt proves it derived the same keys; the driver checks it ( Config::verify_eckey_receipt , on by default). The derivation is printed in AN12543 pp. 22-23 and 72-73 but has no test vector yet, so the session is off by default : without the build flag SE05X_ENABLE_ECKEY_SESSION=1 , eckey::Session::Open() returns Unsupported and sends nothing. Turn it on only after checking the handshake against your chip. UserID session ¶ A UserID session has no secure messaging: the UserID and every command travel in clear. On the SE051 a UserID defaults to unlimited attempts (AN13030 p. 155). The driver refuses an unlimited counter, counts attempts on the host too ( Config::auth_attempt_limit ) and refuses secret operations over a UserID session unless platform SCP03 is open. Rules the channels keep ¶ A failed handshake wipes the session keys at once, but a session that failed after CreateSession cannot be closed: the applet closes only a fully set-up session (AN12543 3.6.5, p. 35). The channel sends no CloseSession then and sets NeedsReselect() ; select the applet again (or reset the chip) to drop the half-open session. At the levels with R-MAC, every 9000 answer is MAC-checked, short ones too, in constant time. An error status word carries no R-MAC and is not authenticated: the channel accepts it only as the two bytes alone and closes on anything else. At the levels without R-MAC no answer is authenticated. One exception: a command that ends the applet session ( DeleteAll ) is answered without secure messaging (AN12543 4.20.5, p. 154); the session that sent it accepts a bare 9000 for that command only, and is then gone. The levels are CMac (0x01), CMacCDecrypt (0x03), CMacRMac (0x11) and Full (0x33). The facade counts only what it needs: authenticated answers ( CMacRMac or Full , Device::AnswersAuthenticated() ) for keys, counters and verification, and encryption both ways ( Full , Device::TrafficConfidential() ) for ECDH and secret data. CMac alone authenticates the commands, not the answers, so the facade refuses those calls over it. Counters never rewind; a channel is never resumed after a reset. Errata JOS.2 (SE050 errata 3.13, pp. 11-12): inside platform SCP03 the chip does not advance the encryption counter for a command without data. The errata's workaround appends data to such commands; the driver does not, it follows the chip's rule instead ( scp03::ChannelParams::jos2_counter_rule , on by default). Applet sessions advance the counter on every command. A lost frame, a failed MAC check or any recovery rung past a block resend under a session or platform SCP03 ends the stack: the call returns the error and the device is NeedsReopen until Device::Recover() selects the applet again and opens platform SCP03 again. Once platform SCP03 was open, no command goes out in the clear before that. An applet session inside platform SCP03 is two secure-messaging layers: the session wraps the command, the frame goes into ProcessSessionCmd, and platform SCP03 wraps that again. The 940-byte EdDSA input fits both (the wire limit kMaxCommandApdu is 1108 bytes); a UserID session takes 919 bytes (AN12543 pp. 103-104).

docs.text: Security model ¶ What the chip protects, what it does not, where the trust boundaries are and what this driver adds. Read this before you choose a secure channel or write a provisioning plan. Datasheet sections this page relies on Common Criteria EAL 6+ for hardware and OS: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 2.2 Key features, p. 3 SE051 Common Criteria EAL 6+ for hardware and OS: NXP SE051 Rev. 2.0, 2.2 Key features, p. 3 SE052 Common Criteria EAL 6+ for hardware and OS: NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, 3.1 Product-specific features, p. 3 Attestation: hash of the command, no freshness echo (applet 7.x): NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Attestation, p. 19 APDU throughput limit on the SE052F: NXP AN13904 Rev. 1.0, APDU throughput limit, p. 28 PERSO applet needs no authentication: anyone can change the address: NXP AN13015 Rev. 1.4, Deleting the PERSO applet, p. 19 Platform SCP03 with AES-128 and AES-256; keys in plain files are insecure: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, Platform SCP03, p. 152 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Trust boundaries Figure description and sources Three zones from right to left. Inside the chip: the private keys, the policies, the counters, the RNG and the attestation key; the chip enforces every access rule. The bus between host and chip carries APDUs in clear unless a secure channel (platform SCP03, an AESKey or an ECKey session) wraps them; anyone with a probe on SDA and SCL sees and can inject plain traffic. The host MCU runs this driver, which is a courier: it holds no long-term secret except the platform SCP03 keys, and those only as handles in the crypto port. The verifier, far left, checks attestations and signatures with public keys only. Each arrow says what crosses the boundary. Drawn from: inc/se05x_ports.hpp ; inc/se05x_secret.hpp ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/trust-boundaries.py . In plain words ¶ If someone... ...can they? Why not, or what you do copies the flash of a stolen device not the keys or the Secret data, if the platform SCP03 keys are in a key store a flash copy cannot read the keys and secrets live in the chip, which never returns a private key; whoever holds the platform SCP03 keys can open the chip like your firmware ( Store a secret ) clips a probe on SDA and SCL read or change nothing, once RequirePlatformScp has been applied and your firmware opens platform SCP03 at Full every command is encrypted and MACed and every 9000 answer MACed and encrypted; an error status word is not authenticated, so a probe can turn a success into an error; before RequirePlatformScp the chip also takes plain commands from the probe (see below) ( Secure channel ) replays an old answer of the chip not inside an open channel, and not as an attestation SCP03 MACs chain over the session; attested answers carry a fresh host nonce and a later timestamp. A plain answer outside a channel can be replayed installs an old firmware image no, if you check the floor at boot the counter only counts up and cannot be deleted ( Anti-rollback ) moves your device's identity to another device no the private key cannot leave the chip ( Device identity ) runs their own code on your MCU use the chip as your code could, while it runs keep policies narrow and secrets inside the chip; the chip cannot tell your code from theirs floods the chip with commands (SE052F) stop it until a reset count APDUs with the budget ( HRoT cookbook ); the facade admits a call only when its worst case fits under the limit changes the chip's lifecycle only with the session the operation needs irreversible operations are compiled out by default and need a plan and a typed confirmation ( Provisioning ) Before the channel is open The chip's default is platform SCP03 not required (AN12543 3.14). Until RequirePlatformScp has been applied, a probe on the bus can break your firmware's session and send plain commands of its own: read and rewrite Protection::Public data and certificates, and create objects in the slots of your plan before your firmware does. The facade's Find and CreateCounter refuse objects it did not make with its own exact policy, and Protection::Secret data and facade keys refuse use without secure messaging, but a planted object still blocks its slot. Provision in a trusted place and apply RequirePlatformScp before the device leaves it. Assets ¶ Asset Where it lives Protected by Private and secret keys Secure objects in the chip The chip: no command returns a private key; policies decide every use Attestation key Provisioned by the vendor in the chip The chip; ORIGIN_PROVISIONED objects cannot be deleted Policies Stored with each object The chip checks them on every command Counters, PCRs Secure objects The chip: increment-only, extend-only Platform SCP03 keys (host copy) Your crypto port, as KeyRef handles Your platform: a key store, a protected flash, a hardware engine Session keys The driver's channel object while it is open Wiped at close, reset, error Data in flight The I2C bus Nothing, unless a secure channel wraps it Trust boundaries ¶ Chip and bus. Everything on SDA and SCL is visible and changeable by anyone with a probe. Plain APDUs reveal what you sign and what you read, and can be replayed or altered. Platform SCP03, an AESKey session or an ECKey session encrypt and authenticate the commands and replies. Driver and host. The driver is a courier: it builds frames, runs the secure channel and checks what comes back. It holds no long-term secret except the platform SCP03 keys, and those only as handles your crypto port resolves. A compromised host can use the chip as it pleases while it is compromised (an oracle), but it cannot extract a key the policies keep inside. Chip and verifier. A remote party trusts a value because the chip signed it (attestation) with a key whose certificate chains to the vendor. The verifier needs public keys only. Threats and answers ¶ Threat The chip's answer The driver's answer Read a key off the bus Keys never leave the chip No API reads a private key; strict policies forbid it Sniff or alter APDUs SCP03 and session encryption, MAC Config::scp_policy ( Require for a root of trust: Auto decides from an unauthenticated answer); R-MAC checked on every reply, short ones too, except the bare 9000 of a command that ends the applet session ( DeleteAll ), which the chip sends without secure messaging and which is therefore not authenticated (A22); the facade needs R-MAC for results and encryption both ways for secrets Replay an attestation Format 1 echoes a nonce; format 2 signs the command (AN12543 p. 19) A fresh host nonce per request (never the attested chip's RNG), byte-for-byte compare, a timestamp later than the last accepted, across reopens Brute-force a UserID Attempt counter, if set No infinite counters; host-side attempt limit ( auth_attempt_limit ) Use a key through a stolen host Policies tie use to an authentication object Facade keys require secure messaging and name the default session and the session they were made in (A20); a stricter binding names an authentication object in a policy built with PolicyBuilder::For() Lock the chip by flooding it Throughput limit SW 0x66A6 (AN13904 p. 28) ApduBudget counts commands across reopens and refuses loops Change the I2C address or protocol (SE051) The PERSO applet has no authentication until it is deleted (AN13015 p. 19) perso::Perso::Probe() warns; writes need a confirmation Brick the chip by mistake Some lifecycle settings are permanent Compiled out by default; Plan and Confirmation ( Irreversible operations ); immutable files and UserID objects only through a plan Roll back an anti-rollback floor A counter only counts up The facade's counter policy forbids delete, and the counter is created with its value in one command Default platform keys The vendor publishes them for each configuration None in this repository; your keys enter through the crypto port only What the chip does not protect ¶ Your host software. A host that runs an attacker's code can sign anything the policies let it sign. The bus without a channel. The chip's default is platform SCP03 not required (SetPlatformSCPRequest, AN12543 p. 75); except in a configuration that requires it, plain commands work until you require it. Availability. A held I2C bus (errata I2C.1) or the throughput limit stops the chip until a reset or a power cycle; plan the reset wiring ( Hardware ). Key backup. A key generated inside is gone when the chip is gone. Back up by design (a second chip, a certificate you can re-issue), not by export. Certification is the chip's, not the driver's ¶ The SE050F is certified FIPS 140-2 and the SE052F FIPS 140-3 Level 3 (vendor data sheets and AN14671); the hardware and OS of each chip are Common Criteria EAL 6+ (SE050 data sheet 2.2 Key features, p. 3; SE051 data sheet 2.2 Key features, p. 3; SE052 data sheet 3.1 Product-specific features, p. 3). Those certificates cover the chip in its documented configuration. This driver is not certified; using it does not make a product compliant. The reference crypto in the driver is for tests and bring-up only and is not hardened against side channels beyond constant-time comparison. Rules the driver enforces ¶ The full rule list (S-01 to S-17: wiping, logging, policies, waits, recovery, channels, attestation, irreversible operations, the APDU budget) is on Safety rules .

A held I2C bus (errata I2C.1) or the throughput limit stops the chip until a reset or a power cycle; plan the reset wiring ( Hardware ). Key backup. A key generated inside is gone when the chip is gone. Back up by design (a second chip, a certificate you can re-issue), not by export.
docs.title: What the chip does not protect

docs.text: The SE050F is certified FIPS 140-2 and the SE052F FIPS 140-3 Level 3 (vendor data sheets and AN14671); the hardware and OS of each chip are Common Criteria EAL 6+ (SE050 data sheet 2.2 Key features, p. 3; SE051 data sheet 2.2 Key features, p. 3; SE052 data sheet 3.1 Product-specific features, p. 3). Those certificates cover the chip in its documented configuration. This driver is not certified; using it does not make a product compliant. The reference crypto in the driver is for tests and bring-up only and is not hardened against side channels beyond constant-time comparison.
docs.title: Certification is the chip's, not the driver's

docs.text: Errors and status words ¶ Every call returns se05x::Result<T> : an Error , and a Detail with the chip's raw status word ( sw ), the command, the layer that failed, a layer step and, after a failed authentication, the attempts left. This page lists every Error , what to do about it, and how the chip's status words map to it. Datasheet sections this page relies on APP.1 attestation over 1024 bytes, APP.2 CloseSession without a session: NXP SE050_Erratasheet Rev. 1.0, 3.5, 3.6, p. 9 NXP flavour S-blocks: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Table 9, p. 7 Status words and APDU encoding: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Table 21 and the APDU encoding rules, p. 49 APDU throughput limit on the SE052F: NXP AN13904 Rev. 1.0, APDU throughput limit, p. 28 APDU throughput limit, SW 0x66A6: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, 2.12 and 10.16.6, p. 10 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Errors ¶ Error Value Meaning What to do Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Open() has not succeeded, or Close() ran Call Open() InvalidArgument 2 An argument or Config field is out of range; nothing was sent Fix the argument; Validate(config) checks a Config Bus 3 The I2C port failed (arbitration, framing) Check wiring and pull-ups; the ladder has already retried Timeout 4 A bounded wait ended (block waiting time, WTX budget, command timeout) Raise the class timeout in Config::timeouts only if the command is slow by nature DeviceIdMismatch 5 The chip is not an SE05x with the IoT applet Check the part, the address and the flavour Crc 6 A frame failed its CRC and the resend budget is spent Signal integrity, bus speed, flavour Busy 7 A command is in flight One command at a time (errata I2C.1); serialise the callers DeviceFault 8 The chip reported an internal error Read Detail::sw ; reset if it repeats Unsupported 9 The capability gate refuses the command for this chip Read the capabilities; choose another variant or call BufferTooSmall 16 A caller buffer or a frame budget is too small Give a larger span WrongState 17 Locked applet, SCP required, no session, or the wrong object class Open the session or channel the command needs Nack 18 The chip did not acknowledge its address Absent, still booting, or held in deep power-down BusStuck 19 SCL or SDA held low Power cycle: ENA (SE050, SE051) or the supply TransportDead 20 The recovery ladder is spent Close() , check the hardware, Open() FrameError 21 A malformed T=1 block Flavour mismatch is the usual cause Resynced 22 The link recovered; the command was not repeated Authenticate again, then repeat if it is safe to NeedsReselect 23 The applet must be selected again Call Device::Recover() ; sessions are gone ObjectNotFound 24 No object with that id Provision it, or check the id ObjectExists 25 An object with that id exists Use Find() or another slot PolicyDenied 26 The object's policy does not allow this. From the facade (layer Hrot ): the answers are not authenticated (no R-MAC layer) for a key, counter or verification, or the traffic is not encrypted both ways for ECDH or secret data (nothing sent); or CheckFloor found a version below the floor. From the chip (0x6986): also an object made by the facade in another applet session (A20) Open the session the policy names; for the facade, open platform SCP03 at CMacRMac or Full ( Full for secrets), or an AESKey session PolicyInvalid 27 A policy was refused, by the builder or the chip Use rules valid for the class and generation AuthFailed 28 Authentication failed; attempts_left when known Check the credential; do not loop AuthLocked 29 The credential is blocked, or the host-side attempt limit is reached Stop; a blocked credential needs its owner ConditionsNotSatisfied 30 SW 0x6985 with no better name in this context Read Detail ; often a missing precondition MemoryFull 31 No room for the object Delete objects; FreeMemory() reports what is left SecureChannelError 32 A MAC, cryptogram, padding or counter check failed; the channel is closed Re-open the channel; investigate if it repeats AttestationInvalid 33 Freshness, timestamp or signature failed; from hrot::Device::VerifySignature , the signature does not verify Treat the value as untrusted Counterfeit 34 The unique id or certificate chain does not match Treat the chip as untrusted IrreversibleNotConfirmed 35 An irreversible operation without its plan or confirmation; also Execute of a WriteUserId or of a WriteBinary that creates an immutable file See Irreversible operations ChipSwUnknown 36 A status word the driver has no mapping for Read Detail::sw and report it CryptoFailure 37 The crypto port failed or refused a key handle Check your crypto port NotImplemented 38 Not returned by any call of this version (kept for a later layer) Report it: it is a bug ThroughputLimited 39 SW 0x66A6: the chip refuses every command until it is reset; from the facade (layer Hrot ): the call would pass the APDU budget, nothing was sent Device: it reset the chip once and selected the applet again; re-authenticate and slow down. Facade: wait for the window to pass ToString(Error) gives each name. The values are a stable contract: 0 to 9 are the base set every driver shares. Layers ¶ Detail::layer says which layer produced the error; Detail::step is that layer's own step number. Layer Value Produced by step None 0 Success 0 Port 1 A port hook (bus, clock, reset, crypto) 0 T1 2 The T=1 link The frame or ladder step Apdu 3 Encoding, TLV parsing, status-word mapping 0 Scp03 4 Platform SCP03 or an AESKey session The handshake or unwrap step EcKey 5 An ECKey session The handshake step Gp 6 The card manager 0 Device 7 The command layer (gate, roles, sessions, recovery) The device step Hrot 8 The facade 1 refused before sending (closed, budget, no secure messaging); 2 an argument; 3 below the floor; 4 a signature that does not verify; 5 another chip's identity Pki 9 The optional PKI layer ( PKI ) The pki::Reason ( pki::ReasonOf(detail) ) Status words ¶ The applet's generic status words are AN12543 Table 21 (p. 49); the document says its per-command lists are not exhaustive. Rows marked "not in Table 21" come from other sources, named in the row. The same word can mean different things by command, so apdu::StatusToError(command, sw) maps it in context. SW The chip says Usual Error 9000 Success Ok 6700 Wrong length InvalidArgument 6982 Security status not satisfied PolicyDenied 6984 Data invalid: policy set invalid for the object PolicyInvalid 6985 Conditions of use not satisfied ConditionsNotSatisfied , or by context NeedsReselect , MemoryFull (3.x), PolicyInvalid 6986 Command not allowed: access denied by the object policy PolicyDenied 6A80 Wrong data (the text on p. 37 also uses it for an invalid policy) PolicyInvalid on creation, else InvalidArgument 6A82 Not in Table 21; the driver's contract maps it as not found ObjectNotFound 6A84 Not enough memory, transient or persistent MemoryFull 66A6 APDU throughput limit reached (AN13904 p. 28) ThroughputLimited 6D00 Not in Table 21; the vendor middleware reselects the applet on it (AN13030 p. 10) NeedsReselect Contexts the driver knows: 0x6985 after CloseSession without a session leaves the applet unusable until it is selected again (errata APP.2, p. 9): the driver never sends that CloseSession and maps the word to NeedsReselect . 0x6985 on ExchangeSessionData means an invalid session policy; on VerifySessionUserID a wrong UserID ( AuthFailed ). Responses above 1024 bytes are refused on the SE050 (errata APP.1, p. 9); the driver checks the size first. AN12543 names both 6A80 (p. 37) and 6984 (Table 21) for an invalid policy; both map to PolicyInvalid on a create. T=1 control blocks ¶ S-block requests and their responses (UM11225 Table 9, p. 7; GPC_SPE_172 Table 4-4, p. 34): Request Response NXP flavour GP flavour C0 E0 Resync Resync C1 E1 Information field size Information field size C2 E2 Abort Abort C3 E3 Waiting time extension Waiting time extension C4 E4 CIP C5 E5 End of APDU session (power saving) C6 E6 Chip reset Release (power saving) C7 E7 Get ATR CF EF Interface soft reset Software reset The same code C6 means a chip reset in one flavour and a release in the other: the link never sends it before the flavour is known.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the chip, vectors from the specifications and from the pinned NXP middleware (a test oracle, never a dependency), compile-fail tests, fuzzers, compiled documentation, an install test, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_contract.cpp The frozen contract: every header is included, every public type and constant is asserted; with the irreversible flag off and on tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value has a name tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port that is not a port, an irreversible command through Execute , a wrong confirmation, a slot out of range tests/fuzz/ The ten fuzz targets; CTest replays their corpora tests/docs/ The snippets the pages show, compiled tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds a consumer The model stands alone ¶ The chip model in tests/model/ is written from the documents, not from the driver: a chain T1Target -> ScpTarget -> ChipModel implements ApduHandler , with knobs for the open questions ( crc_swapped , gp_flavour , throttle_enabled , throttle_after ). It includes no driver header other than the frozen interface, so a wrong constant in the driver is caught by the model and the reverse. A behaviour found on hardware becomes a fault in the model first, then a fix. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus. The fuzz targets corrupt what the chip sends and check the promises after every call: a failed call returns a defined Error , nothing is sent before Open() , a secret is never logged. Ten targets run: fuzz_apdu_response , fuzz_atr_cip , fuzz_contract_stub (the shared byte parsers), fuzz_device_sequence , fuzz_hrot_sequence , fuzz_pki_der , fuzz_pki_x509 , fuzz_policy_parse , fuzz_scp03_unwrap and fuzz_t1_frame . Each target also builds without libFuzzer as a replay and CTest runs its corpus. Mutation ¶ tools/mutants/mutants.py applies one-edit mutants to a copy of inc/ , src/ and tests/ , builds the host tests with irreversible operations off and on, and runs them. Every mutant must be killed: by a failing test or a static_assert . The unedited tree is built and run first; if it fails, the run stops, because a failing test would otherwise count as a kill. cmake -S . -B build -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON # generates se05x_version.h SE05X_GENERATED = build/se05x_generated tools/mutants/mutants.py --jobs 8 tools/mutants/mutants.py --list # the catalogue, active and pending tools/mutants/mutants.py --selftest # every pattern of every catalogue is in its file SE05X_GENERATED = build/se05x_generated tools/mutants/mutants.py --all # the full lists of every area The script holds a core set per area; the full lists are tools/mutants/transport.txt , apdu.txt , channels.txt , device.txt , hrot.txt (the facade, the irreversible plans and the verified attested read) and pki.txt (the optional PKI layer); --catalogue FILE runs one, --all every one. No entry is pending: every layer is built. Mutants build with the library's bounds checks, so an out-of-range access traps, and a run that hangs past ten minutes counts as a kill. Policy: Every comparison, counter, constant and status-word mapping that guards a safety rule (S-01 to S-17) has a mutant: the CRC polynomial and order, N(S), the chaining bit, the WTX and retry caps, the single-flight and empty-write guards, the MAC, receipt, freshness and echoed-command compares, the SCP03 counter, the JOS.2 padding, the wipes, the timestamp order, the policy rules, the capability gate, the role check, the throughput rung and the budget, the confirmation compare and the plan check. A surviving mutant is a finding: it is closed by a test, never by deleting the mutant. An equivalent mutant (another guard covers the same case) is listed with its reason and not run. Mutants of a layer still being built are pending entries with their owner; the release gate ( --strict ) fails while any is left (none is left). The run is per file and part of the first-push evidence; it is not a CI job (it builds the tests once per mutant). MISRA C++:2023 ¶ The CI job MISRA analyses every translation unit against the handbook's compliance matrix at the high level; tools/misra_lint.py checks the defect classes earlier scans found, in the preflight. A guideline the code cannot follow gets a deviation record: the guideline number, the file and line, why, what makes it safe, the approver. The records live in this section. Guideline Where Why Mitigation Approved none recorded Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( se05x_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/se05x.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. The MISRA scan, rehearsed locally ¶ The scan runs only in CI, and a first push has paid for the same few findings again and again. tools/misra_lint.py (standard-library Python, no build) catches those classes before the push; tools/preflight.sh runs it as the misra-lint step, which cannot be skipped, and its --selftest as misra-lint-selftest . It reads the C++ files ( *.hpp , *.cpp , *.ipp ) of inc/ , src/ , tests/ and examples/ and prints file:line Rule N.N.N message : Rule Reported Severity 9.4.1 an if ... else if chain that does not end in a plain else (at the last else if ) error 7.0.3 arithmetic, comparison or conversion on a char : c - '0' , c >= '0' , token[0] == '-' , static_cast<char>(byte) error 0.1.2 a call statement that drops the result of a function the tree declares with a class return type error (scalar result: warning) 13.3.3 a function whose declaration and definition use different parameter names error KB-CPP-012 an include in inc/ or src/ outside the driver's library subset error 8.0.1 an operand of a logical and / or that is a comparison or bitwise expression and is not parenthesised warning Severity. An error fails the preflight; a warning is printed and counted in the summary line ( misra_lint: N file(s), E error(s), W warning(s) ) and does not. A finding is an error only when its rule is one the CI scan blocks on and it is in inc/ or src/ ; every finding in tests/ or examples/ is a warning, as are 8.0.1 everywhere and --void-casts ( (void)expr; , which the scan accepts). --strict turns every warning into an error, for a reviewer who wants the whole list. This split is derived from CI evidence, not from the rule text: the scan reported 7.0.3, 9.4.1, 0.1.2 and 13.3.3 as failure and 8.0.1 as warning , only failure annotations fail the job, all findings listed were in inc/ and src/ , and drivers whose CI is green still carry else if chains in tests/ . Revisit it if CodeQL is ever seen blocking on a finding in tests/ or examples/ , or on 8.0.1: move that rule or folder into the error set ( TRACED and the severities in tools/misra_lint.py ). The check is a token scan without types: it reports what it can decide and stays silent otherwise, so a clean run does not replace the scan, but an error is an error. Fix the code: compare characters through a table or std::array<char, 1> equality, convert a byte with std::bit_cast<char> , end the chain in else , give the declaration and the definition the same parameter names, use the returned value or discard it with static_cast<void> . A deliberate exception carries the deviation the scan reads ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-...) on the line before) or // misra-lint: ignore 8.0.1 on the line. --strict-precedence ( a < b + 1 ) reports more 8.0.1. The include subset is read from handbook_check.py of a ci-tools checkout ( CI_TOOLS_DIR , default ../ci-tools ), so the two never differ; without the checkout the built-in list of ADR-0017 applies. The preflight also runs that handbook_check.py itself (the handbook-check step; skipped, with the reason named, only when the checkout or PyYAML is missing), lints tests/install_consumer/main.cpp with clang-tidy like every other C++ file (it is built by its own CMake project, so it is not in the host build's compilation database), and checks the first-push gitlink: after git add -A , examples/esp32/scripts must be a gitlink (mode 160000). Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target se05x_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . docs.text: How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the chip, vectors from the specifications and from the pinned NXP middleware (a test oracle, never a dependency), compile-fail tests, fuzzers, compiled documentation, an install test, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request.
docs.title: Testing and CI

docs.text: The tests build the real driver with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_contract.cpp The frozen contract: every header is included, every public type and constant is asserted; with the irreversible flag off and on tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value has a name tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port that is not a port, an irreversible command through Execute , a wrong confirmation, a slot out of range tests/fuzz/ The ten fuzz targets; CTest replays their corpora tests/docs/ The snippets the pages show, compiled tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds a consumer
docs.title: Host tests

docs.text: The chip model in tests/model/ is written from the documents, not from the driver: a chain T1Target -> ScpTarget -> ChipModel implements ApduHandler , with knobs for the open questions ( crc_swapped , gp_flavour , throttle_enabled , throttle_after ). It includes no driver header other than the frozen interface, so a wrong constant in the driver is caught by the model and the reverse. A behaviour found on hardware becomes a fault in the model first, then a fix.
docs.title: The model stands alone

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus. The fuzz targets corrupt what the chip sends and check the promises after every call: a failed call returns a defined Error , nothing is sent before Open() , a secret is never logged. Ten targets run: fuzz_apdu_response , fuzz_atr_cip , fuzz_contract_stub (the shared byte parsers), fuzz_device_sequence , fuzz_hrot_sequence , fuzz_pki_der , fuzz_pki_x509 , fuzz_policy_parse , fuzz_scp03_unwrap and fuzz_t1_frame . Each target also builds without libFuzzer as a replay and CTest runs its corpus.
docs.title: Fuzz tests

docs.text: tools/mutants/mutants.py applies one-edit mutants to a copy of inc/ , src/ and tests/ , builds the host tests with irreversible operations off and on, and runs them. Every mutant must be killed: by a failing test or a static_assert . The unedited tree is built and run first; if it fails, the run stops, because a failing test would otherwise count as a kill. cmake -S . -B build -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON # generates se05x_version.h SE05X_GENERATED = build/se05x_generated tools/mutants/mutants.py --jobs 8 tools/mutants/mutants.py --list # the catalogue, active and pending tools/mutants/mutants.py --selftest # every pattern of every catalogue is in its file SE05X_GENERATED = build/se05x_generated tools/mutants/mutants.py --all # the full lists of every area The script holds a core set per area; the full lists are tools/mutants/transport.txt , apdu.txt , channels.txt , device.txt , hrot.txt (the facade, the irreversible plans and the verified attested read) and pki.txt (the optional PKI layer); --catalogue FILE runs one, --all every one. No entry is pending: every layer is built. Mutants build with the library's bounds checks, so an out-of-range access traps, and a run that hangs past ten minutes counts as a kill. Policy: Every comparison, counter, constant and status-word mapping that guards a safety rule (S-01 to S-17) has a mutant: the CRC polynomial and order, N(S), the chaining bit, the WTX and retry caps, the single-flight and empty-write guards, the MAC, receipt, freshness and echoed-command compares, the SCP03 counter, the JOS.2 padding, the wipes, the timestamp order, the policy rules, the capability gate, the role check, the throughput rung and the budget, the confirmation compare and the plan check. A surviving mutant is a finding: it is closed by a test, never by deleting the mutant. An equivalent mutant (another guard covers the same case) is listed with its reason and not run. Mutants of a layer still being built are pending entries with their owner; the release gate ( --strict ) fails while any is left (none is left). The run is per file and part of the first-push evidence; it is not a CI job (it builds the tests once per mutant).
docs.title: Mutation

docs.text: The CI job MISRA analyses every translation unit against the handbook's compliance matrix at the high level; tools/misra_lint.py checks the defect classes earlier scans found, in the preflight. A guideline the code cannot follow gets a deviation record: the guideline number, the file and line, why, what makes it safe, the approver. The records live in this section. Guideline Where Why Mitigation Approved none recorded
docs.title: MISRA C++:2023

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DSE05X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( se05x_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/se05x.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.
docs.title: Quality gates

docs.text: The scan runs only in CI, and a first push has paid for the same few findings again and again. tools/misra_lint.py (standard-library Python, no build) catches those classes before the push; tools/preflight.sh runs it as the misra-lint step, which cannot be skipped, and its --selftest as misra-lint-selftest . It reads the C++ files ( *.hpp , *.cpp , *.ipp ) of inc/ , src/ , tests/ and examples/ and prints file:line Rule N.N.N message : Rule Reported Severity 9.4.1 an if ... else if chain that does not end in a plain else (at the last else if ) error 7.0.3 arithmetic, comparison or conversion on a char : c - '0' , c >= '0' , token[0] == '-' , static_cast<char>(byte) error 0.1.2 a call statement that drops the result of a function the tree declares with a class return type error (scalar result: warning) 13.3.3 a function whose declaration and definition use different parameter names error KB-CPP-012 an include in inc/ or src/ outside the driver's library subset error 8.0.1 an operand of a logical and / or that is a comparison or bitwise expression and is not parenthesised warning Severity. An error fails the preflight; a warning is printed and counted in the summary line ( misra_lint: N file(s), E error(s), W warning(s) ) and does not. A finding is an error only when its rule is one the CI scan blocks on and it is in inc/ or src/ ; every finding in tests/ or examples/ is a warning, as are 8.0.1 everywhere and --void-casts ( (void)expr; , which the scan accepts). --strict turns every warning into an error, for a reviewer who wants the whole list. This split is derived from CI evidence, not from the rule text: the scan reported 7.0.3, 9.4.1, 0.1.2 and 13.3.3 as failure and 8.0.1 as warning , only failure annotations fail the job, all findings listed were in inc/ and src/ , and drivers whose CI is green still carry else if chains in tests/ . Revisit it if CodeQL is ever seen blocking on a finding in tests/ or examples/ , or on 8.0.1: move that rule or folder into the error set ( TRACED and the severities in tools/misra_lint.py ). The check is a token scan without types: it reports what it can decide and stays silent otherwise, so a clean run does not replace the scan, but an error is an error. Fix the code: compare characters through a table or std::array<char, 1> equality, convert a byte with std::bit_cast<char> , end the chain in else , give the declaration and the definition the same parameter names, use the returned value or discard it with static_cast<void> . A deliberate exception carries the deviation the scan reads ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-...) on the line before) or // misra-lint: ignore 8.0.1 on the line. --strict-precedence ( a < b + 1 ) reports more 8.0.1. The include subset is read from handbook_check.py of a ci-tools checkout ( CI_TOOLS_DIR , default ../ci-tools ), so the two never differ; without the checkout the built-in list of ADR-0017 applies. The preflight also runs that handbook_check.py itself (the handbook-check step; skipped, with the reason named, only when the checkout or PyYAML is missing), lints tests/install_consumer/main.cpp with clang-tidy like every other C++ file (it is built by its own CMake project, so it is not in the host build's compilation database), and checks the first-push gitlink: after git add -A , examples/esp32/scripts must be a gitlink (mode 160000).

docs.text: Transport: T=1 over I2C ¶ How a command reaches the chip: the I2C rules, the block format of both T=1 flavours, the control blocks, the waits and the recovery ladder. The layer is se05x::t1::Link ; its numbers are in inc/se05x_wire.hpp . Datasheet sections this page relies on Power-down and deep power-down modes: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 5 Power-saving modes, p. 9 Wake-up from power-down may need a retransmission: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, Table 14 notes 4 and 5, p. 19 SE051 power-saving modes: NXP SE051 Rev. 2.0, 5 Power-saving modes, p. 11 SE052 power-down by RELEASE and deep power-down by S-block 0xDF: NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, 10 Power-saving modes, p. 7 SE052 CIP bytes in the configuration: NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, Table 12 Configuration parameters, p. 17 SE052 tDPD: no access for 300 us after a deep power-down: NXP SE052 Rev. 1.5, Table 15 Electrical AC characteristics, tDPD, p. 22 I2C.1 lock-up after a second command, I2C.2 no empty frame: NXP SE050_Erratasheet Rev. 1.0, 3.1, 3.2, p. 7 NXP flavour block: NAD, PCB, LEN, INF, CRC: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Table 1, Tables 3 and 4, p. 5 NXP flavour I-block and R-block PCB: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Tables 5 to 7, p. 6 NXP flavour S-blocks: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Table 9, p. 7 NXP flavour ATR: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Tables 11 to 13, p. 9 Retransmissions, WTX and soft reset rules: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Error handling and retransmission, p. 11 One block per I2C write, no repeated start: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, I2C framing, p. 13 Polling with one-byte reads after MPOT: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Polling, p. 14 Default SEGT, MPOT and power wake-up time: NXP UM11225 Rev. 1.2, Table 14, p. 19 GP flavour I2C: polling, guard times, clock stretching: GlobalPlatform GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, I2C physical layer, p. 23 GP flavour default IFSC, BWT and power wake time: GlobalPlatform GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, Default values, p. 31 GP flavour block, NAD 21/12, two-byte LEN, CRC example BDA4: GlobalPlatform GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, Table 4-1, p. 33 GP flavour PCB and S-block codes: GlobalPlatform GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, Table 4-4, p. 34 GP flavour CIP: GlobalPlatform GPC_SPE_172 v1.0, Tables 4-6 to 4-9, p. 36 WTX host timeout at least 4 s; NXP mode is the default: NXP AN13904 Rev. 1.0, WTX and T=1 mode, p. 27 T=1 chip reset and deep power-down: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, 10.16, p. 281 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The block ¶ One T=1 block on the bus Figure description and sources One block on the I2C bus, in the order its bytes are sent, for each flavour the driver speaks. The NXP flavour (UM11225) has NAD 0x5A from the host and 0xA5 from the chip, a one-byte LEN and at most 254 bytes of INF. The GlobalPlatform flavour (GPC_SPE_172) has NAD 0x21 and 0x12, a two-byte big-endian LEN and up to 4089 bytes of INF. Both end with a CRC-16 over NAD to INF; in the GP flavour it is CRC-16/X-25 sent most significant byte first (the document's example block ends in BDA4); UM11225 gives neither the polynomial's byte order nor an example, so the link tries both orders and keeps the first that checks. The PCB byte tells the three kinds of block apart. Every number is read from inc/se05x_wire.hpp. Drawn from: inc/se05x_wire.hpp kUm11225Frame, kGpFrame, kGpExampleCrc ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/t1-frame.py . Two flavours exist and they do not interoperate: NXP (UM11225) GlobalPlatform (GPC_SPE_172) NAD host to chip, chip to host 0x5A , 0xA5 0x21 , 0x12 LEN 1 byte, INF up to 254 2 bytes big endian, INF up to 4089 CRC CRC-16 of ISO 7816-3; byte order not stated CRC-16/X-25, MSB first; example BDA4 Identification ATR (S-block C7, or the reply to a soft reset) CIP (S-block C4) Power saving End of APDU session C5 Release C6 Defaults before the ATR or CIP SEGT 10 us, MPOT 1 ms, power wake 5 ms IFSC 8, IFSD 64, BWT 300 ms, power wake 25 ms Which flavour a chip speaks: the SE051 detects it from the first frame it sees (SE051 data sheet 4.1.2, p. 9) and can have it fixed by its PERSO setting (AN13015 p. 49); SE052F NXP mode by default per AN13904 p. 27, while its data sheet's configuration table lists the GP 0.39 flavour (SE052 p. 18); SE050 not stated. So Config::flavour defaults to TransportFlavour::Auto : the link tries the NXP form for half of the ATR poll budget ( Config::atr_poll_budget_ms ), then the GP form for the rest, and keeps the first that checks, CRC byte order included. The NXP form goes first because a chip that locks onto the first frame would otherwise be locked into GP by the probe, and the vendor middleware speaks the NXP form. In the GP flavour the link sends NAD 0x21 and accepts 0x12 or the NXP 0xA5 from the chip: GPC_SPE_172 4.2.1 (p. 33) only recommends 0x12, and the middleware's GP mode expects 0xA5 ( Ambiguities , A17). A stale frame an earlier host left unread decides it sooner: Open() reads it out first, and the NAD it carries names the flavour, which is then the only one tried. A flavour mismatch looks like silence or FrameError ( Troubleshooting ). I2C rules ¶ One block is one I2C write: start, address, the bytes, stop. No repeated start ( kRepeatedStart is false). Never an empty write: an address-only frame makes an SE050 stretch the clock forever (errata I2C.2). The driver never scans the bus; do not scan it yourself. One command in flight: a second command before the reply is read can make the SE050 hold SCL low until a power cycle (errata I2C.1). The link is single flight and returns Busy . While the chip works it NAKs its address. The link polls with reads after the minimum polling time (MPOT, 1 ms by default), up to the block waiting time; a reply may be read in parts, and bytes read past its end are 0xFF . The guard time (SEGT, or RWGT in GP; at least the default 10 us) holds between any two accesses: before every read and every write, the body read after the prologue read included (UM11225 Table 15, p. 20; GPC_SPE_172 3.2.7, p. 28). The one exception is the write right after a NACKed probe for an unread answer (errata I2C.1): a wait there would let the chip's answer arrive just before the write. After a deep power-down by S-block on the SE052 nothing touches the bus for tDPD, 300 us (SE052 data sheet Table 15, p. 22). After an interface soft reset or a chip reset, SDA and SCL stay high (errata I2C.3: a low line there makes the SE050 reset itself after about 1 s, and repeated events lock it). SCL must change before SDA with the data sheet's margin (errata I2C.4): a port requirement, see Porting . States and control blocks ¶ The T=1 link: states and S-blocks Figure description and sources Each box is a LinkState of t1::Link, read from inc/se05x_t1.hpp. Open() reads the ATR or CIP and selects the applet, leaving the link Idle. A command makes it InFlight: one I-block per I2C write (chained when the APDU is longer than IFSC, each part acknowledged by an R-block), then the reply is polled. While in flight the chip may ask for more time with S(WTX request), which the link answers with S(WTX response), counted against Config::wtx_limit; a bad block gets an R-block and is resent at most Config::frame_retries times. A reply returns the link to Idle. A rung of the recovery ladder that resets the chip's context leaves NeedsReselect, which selecting the applet again ends; when the ladder is spent the link is Dead and only Close() and Open() start it again. The S-block codes are the ones of inc/se05x_wire.hpp; 0xC6 is a chip reset in the NXP flavour and RELEASE in the GP one. Drawn from: inc/se05x_t1.hpp LinkState ; inc/se05x_wire.hpp S-block codes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/t1-states.py . Waiting time extension: when the chip needs more than BWT it sends S(WTX request); the link answers S(WTX response) and waits the multiplier times BWT, but at least 4 s (AN13904 p. 27: the host timeout across WTX is at least 4 s). A WTX extends the command's own deadline as well, whatever its class: a Fast command (2 s) that the SE052F keeps alive with a WTX every second, as it does during its FIPS self-test, completes instead of timing out with an unknown outcome (A19). The link never holds SCL across the wait and counts each WTX against Config::wtx_limit . At session open up to 40 WTX requests are allowed ( kSessionOpenWtxAllowance ), as the vendor middleware answers to flush an earlier transaction (AN13030 p. 9). Recovery ¶ The recovery ladder Figure description and sources When an exchange fails the link climbs these rungs in order, read from the Rung enumeration in inc/se05x_t1.hpp, and stops at the first that works. Each rung is bounded and is never repeated without limit. Resending the last block keeps everything. A resync and an interface soft reset keep the chip's state but drop the exchange in progress. Selecting the applet again closes the applet sessions. The chip reset (the NXP-flavour S-block 0xC6, or the reset port in the GP flavour, where 0xC6 means RELEASE) also clears transient objects, and is the only answer to SW 0x66A6. The power cycle needs the reset port (ENA with VOUT wired to VCC on the SE050 and SE051) and is the only cure for errata I2C.1. After any rung past the resend, the driver forgets every session and the caller authenticates again (Error::Resynced). Drawn from: inc/se05x_t1.hpp Rung ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/recovery-ladder.py . UM11225 allows at most ten further attempts after an error before an interface soft reset (p. 11); Config::frame_retries is at most that. The chip-reset rung is the S-block C6 only in the NXP flavour; in the GP flavour C6 is RELEASE, so the rung calls the reset port's Reset() , which must really reset the chip. The power-cycle rung calls the reset port's PowerCycle() ; the driver drives no pin itself. Without a reset port both port rungs are absent. On the SE050 and SE051 RST_N has no effect when only I2C is enabled (SE050 4.2 p. 9, SE051 p. 10), so a port there implements Reset() and PowerCycle() with ENA (VOUT wired to VCC) or a supply switch; on the SE052 Reset() can pulse RST_N (SE052 Table 14, p. 20) ( Porting ). Power saving ¶ Power-down (state kept): entered after the end-of-APDU-session (NXP) or RELEASE (GP) response; a falling edge on SDA wakes it. Waking at 400 kHz or 1 MHz without clock stretching can miss the first block; the chip then asks for a retransmission with an R-block (SE050 Table 14 notes 4 and 5, p. 19). Deep power-down (nothing kept): ENA low on the SE050 and SE051; the S-block 0xDF on the SE052, woken by the next I2C access. Sessions and transient objects are gone afterwards. Device::DeepPowerDown() .

docs.title: Transport: T=1 over I2C

docs.text: One T=1 block on the bus Figure description and sources One block on the I2C bus, in the order its bytes are sent, for each flavour the driver speaks. The NXP flavour (UM11225) has NAD 0x5A from the host and 0xA5 from the chip, a one-byte LEN and at most 254 bytes of INF. The GlobalPlatform flavour (GPC_SPE_172) has NAD 0x21 and 0x12, a two-byte big-endian LEN and up to 4089 bytes of INF. Both end with a CRC-16 over NAD to INF; in the GP flavour it is CRC-16/X-25 sent most significant byte first (the document's example block ends in BDA4); UM11225 gives neither the polynomial's byte order nor an example, so the link tries both orders and keeps the first that checks. The PCB byte tells the three kinds of block apart. Every number is read from inc/se05x_wire.hpp. Drawn from: inc/se05x_wire.hpp kUm11225Frame, kGpFrame, kGpExampleCrc ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/t1-frame.py . Two flavours exist and they do not interoperate: NXP (UM11225) GlobalPlatform (GPC_SPE_172) NAD host to chip, chip to host 0x5A , 0xA5 0x21 , 0x12 LEN 1 byte, INF up to 254 2 bytes big endian, INF up to 4089 CRC CRC-16 of ISO 7816-3; byte order not stated CRC-16/X-25, MSB first; example BDA4 Identification ATR (S-block C7, or the reply to a soft reset) CIP (S-block C4) Power saving End of APDU session C5 Release C6 Defaults before the ATR or CIP SEGT 10 us, MPOT 1 ms, power wake 5 ms IFSC 8, IFSD 64, BWT 300 ms, power wake 25 ms Which flavour a chip speaks: the SE051 detects it from the first frame it sees (SE051 data sheet 4.1.2, p. 9) and can have it fixed by its PERSO setting (AN13015 p. 49); SE052F NXP mode by default per AN13904 p. 27, while its data sheet's configuration table lists the GP 0.39 flavour (SE052 p. 18); SE050 not stated. So Config::flavour defaults to TransportFlavour::Auto : the link tries the NXP form for half of the ATR poll budget ( Config::atr_poll_budget_ms ), then the GP form for the rest, and keeps the first that checks, CRC byte order included. The NXP form goes first because a chip that locks onto the first frame would otherwise be locked into GP by the probe, and the vendor middleware speaks the NXP form. In the GP flavour the link sends NAD 0x21 and accepts 0x12 or the NXP 0xA5 from the chip: GPC_SPE_172 4.2.1 (p. 33) only recommends 0x12, and the middleware's GP mode expects 0xA5 ( Ambiguities , A17). A stale frame an earlier host left unread decides it sooner: Open() reads it out first, and the NAD it carries names the flavour, which is then the only one tried. A flavour mismatch looks like silence or FrameError ( Troubleshooting ).
docs.title: The block

docs.text: One block is one I2C write: start, address, the bytes, stop. No repeated start ( kRepeatedStart is false). Never an empty write: an address-only frame makes an SE050 stretch the clock forever (errata I2C.2). The driver never scans the bus; do not scan it yourself. One command in flight: a second command before the reply is read can make the SE050 hold SCL low until a power cycle (errata I2C.1). The link is single flight and returns Busy . While the chip works it NAKs its address. The link polls with reads after the minimum polling time (MPOT, 1 ms by default), up to the block waiting time; a reply may be read in parts, and bytes read past its end are 0xFF . The guard time (SEGT, or RWGT in GP; at least the default 10 us) holds between any two accesses: before every read and every write, the body read after the prologue read included (UM11225 Table 15, p. 20; GPC_SPE_172 3.2.7, p. 28). The one exception is the write right after a NACKed probe for an unread answer (errata I2C.1): a wait there would let the chip's answer arrive just before the write. After a deep power-down by S-block on the SE052 nothing touches the bus for tDPD, 300 us (SE052 data sheet Table 15, p. 22). After an interface soft reset or a chip reset, SDA and SCL stay high (errata I2C.3: a low line there makes the SE050 reset itself after about 1 s, and repeated events lock it). SCL must change before SDA with the data sheet's margin (errata I2C.4): a port requirement, see Porting .
docs.title: I2C rules

docs.text: The T=1 link: states and S-blocks Figure description and sources Each box is a LinkState of t1::Link, read from inc/se05x_t1.hpp. Open() reads the ATR or CIP and selects the applet, leaving the link Idle. A command makes it InFlight: one I-block per I2C write (chained when the APDU is longer than IFSC, each part acknowledged by an R-block), then the reply is polled. While in flight the chip may ask for more time with S(WTX request), which the link answers with S(WTX response), counted against Config::wtx_limit; a bad block gets an R-block and is resent at most Config::frame_retries times. A reply returns the link to Idle. A rung of the recovery ladder that resets the chip's context leaves NeedsReselect, which selecting the applet again ends; when the ladder is spent the link is Dead and only Close() and Open() start it again. The S-block codes are the ones of inc/se05x_wire.hpp; 0xC6 is a chip reset in the NXP flavour and RELEASE in the GP one. Drawn from: inc/se05x_t1.hpp LinkState ; inc/se05x_wire.hpp S-block codes ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/t1-states.py . Waiting time extension: when the chip needs more than BWT it sends S(WTX request); the link answers S(WTX response) and waits the multiplier times BWT, but at least 4 s (AN13904 p. 27: the host timeout across WTX is at least 4 s). A WTX extends the command's own deadline as well, whatever its class: a Fast command (2 s) that the SE052F keeps alive with a WTX every second, as it does during its FIPS self-test, completes instead of timing out with an unknown outcome (A19). The link never holds SCL across the wait and counts each WTX against Config::wtx_limit . At session open up to 40 WTX requests are allowed ( kSessionOpenWtxAllowance ), as the vendor middleware answers to flush an earlier transaction (AN13030 p. 9).
docs.title: States and control blocks

docs.text: The recovery ladder Figure description and sources When an exchange fails the link climbs these rungs in order, read from the Rung enumeration in inc/se05x_t1.hpp, and stops at the first that works. Each rung is bounded and is never repeated without limit. Resending the last block keeps everything. A resync and an interface soft reset keep the chip's state but drop the exchange in progress. Selecting the applet again closes the applet sessions. The chip reset (the NXP-flavour S-block 0xC6, or the reset port in the GP flavour, where 0xC6 means RELEASE) also clears transient objects, and is the only answer to SW 0x66A6. The power cycle needs the reset port (ENA with VOUT wired to VCC on the SE050 and SE051) and is the only cure for errata I2C.1. After any rung past the resend, the driver forgets every session and the caller authenticates again (Error::Resynced). Drawn from: inc/se05x_t1.hpp Rung ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/recovery-ladder.py . UM11225 allows at most ten further attempts after an error before an interface soft reset (p. 11); Config::frame_retries is at most that. The chip-reset rung is the S-block C6 only in the NXP flavour; in the GP flavour C6 is RELEASE, so the rung calls the reset port's Reset() , which must really reset the chip. The power-cycle rung calls the reset port's PowerCycle() ; the driver drives no pin itself. Without a reset port both port rungs are absent. On the SE050 and SE051 RST_N has no effect when only I2C is enabled (SE050 4.2 p. 9, SE051 p. 10), so a port there implements Reset() and PowerCycle() with ENA (VOUT wired to VCC) or a supply switch; on the SE052 Reset() can pulse RST_N (SE052 Table 14, p. 20) ( Porting ).
docs.title: Recovery

docs.text: Power-down (state kept): entered after the end-of-APDU-session (NXP) or RELEASE (GP) response; a falling edge on SDA wakes it. Waking at 400 kHz or 1 MHz without clock stretching can miss the first block; the chip then asks for a retransmission with an R-block (SE050 Table 14 notes 4 and 5, p. 19). Deep power-down (nothing kept): ENA low on the SE050 and SE051; the S-block 0xDF on the SE052, woken by the next I2C access. Sessions and transient objects are gone afterwards. Device::DeepPowerDown() .
docs.title: Power saving

Open returns Nack or Timeout ¶ The chip is not answering. Supply: VIN (and VCC) 1.62 V to 3.6 V on the SE050 and SE051; VIN 1.65 V to 3.6 V and VDD on the SE052. ENA high on an SE050 or SE051: ENA low is deep power-down, and a chip in it NAKs. Both lines high at power-up: the chip chooses I2C only when SDA and SCL are high at boot (SE050 section 3.4, p. 8). Pull-ups fitted, nothing else on the bus holding a line low. Address 0x48, unless the chip was personalised otherwise (SE051 PERSO, see below). A logic analyser should show the address byte acknowledged after the boot wait; if not, raise Config::boot_wait_ms (the SE050 boot time is not in the documents: ambiguity A8). Bus lock-up: BusStuck, SCL held low ¶ Cause. Errata I2C.1: a second command was written before the first reply was read, and an SE050 with clock stretching holds SCL low until it is power cycled; or errata I2C.2: an address-only write (a bus scan, a probe) and the chip stretches after six more bytes (errata pp. 7-8). Other devices on the bus stop too. Fix. Power cycle the chip: ENA low then high on the SE050 and SE051 with VOUT wired to VCC, or the supply. RST_N does not help on an I2C-only SE050 or SE051. Then remove the cause: never let two tasks use one device without a lock (the driver returns Busy , but a second driver instance or a raw I2C access bypasses it); after a host reset, the chip may still hold an unread reply; the errata's workaround is a read before the first command, and Open() resynchronises the link before it sends one; remove every bus scan and probe call that touches 0x48. Without a reset port the ladder cannot power cycle and ends in TransportDead ; see the minimal circuit on SE050 . The chip resets itself about a second after a soft reset ¶ Errata I2C.3: a line was low during an interface soft reset, so the chip could not detect its interface and reset after about 1 s; several in a row lock it permanently until an applet select succeeds (errata p. 8). Keep both lines high for at least 1 ms after the soft reset. Throughput limit: ThroughputLimited (SW 0x66A6) ¶ The chip refuses every command until it is reset: more than one million APDUs within 34 days on the SE052F (AN13904 p. 28), possibly on the SE051. The device drops every session without sending anything, resets the chip once (the chip-reset rung: the NXP S-block 0xC6, or the reset port in the GP flavour), selects the applet again, opens platform SCP03 again when it was open, and the call returns ThroughputLimited ; the command is not repeated. Re-authenticate. If the chip still answers 0x66A6 to the select, the device stays NeedsReopen and does not reset again. Then find the loop: one APDU per second exceeds the limit in under two weeks. Cache what does not change, read hrot::Device::Budget() , and never poll the chip for time or randomness ( HRoT cookbook ). Flavour mismatch ¶ Symptom. Open() returns FrameError , Crc or DeviceIdMismatch ; a logic analyser shows the chip answering with bytes that do not parse, or nothing after a PERSO write. Cause. The host and the chip speak different T=1 flavours (NXP UM11225 and GlobalPlatform differ in NAD, LEN width and control codes; Transport ). On the SE051 the flavour is a chip-side PERSO setting that takes effect after the next reset (AN13015 p. 49); a mismatch leaves the chip silent to this host. On the SE052 the data sheet's configuration names the GP flavour (p. 18) while AN13904 calls NXP mode the default. Fix. Use TransportFlavour::Auto (the default), which tries both flavours and both CRC orders. If you fixed the flavour in Config , set it to the one the chip uses. On an SE051 whose PERSO applet is still selectable, read I2C_PARAMS with perso::Perso . No zero-length frames ¶ A port that sends an empty write, or a test that probes the address, triggers errata I2C.2. The driver never passes an empty span to Write() ; check your port does not add one (some HALs probe before every transfer). Wake-up from power-down misses the first block ¶ At 400 kHz or 1 MHz without clock stretching, the first block after power-down can arrive before the chip is awake; the chip asks for it again with an R-block (SE050 Table 14 notes 4 and 5, p. 19). The link resends it; this is not an error unless it repeats beyond frame_retries . DeviceIdMismatch ¶ Something answers but is not an SE05x with the IoT applet: a wrong address, a flavour mismatch (above), or an SE051P running a customer applet. A command returns Unsupported ¶ The capability gate refuses it for this chip. Read the capabilities: the applet generation, the version and the feature bits. Some commands exist only on 7.x; the SE052F in FIPS mode has no EdDSA, Montgomery curves, DES or PAKE. Resynced after a call ¶ A recovery rung past a block resend ran: the command was not repeated and every session is gone. Open the session again, then repeat the command if it is safe to. NotImplemented ¶ No call of this version returns it; the value stays in the error model for a layer added later.

docs.text: Where to use it: which variant ¶ The family has three chips, many configurations and two applet generations. This page helps you choose where each fits and which one to order; the per-chip guides ( SE050 , SE051 , SE052 ) cover wiring and what differs. Datasheet sections this page relies on I2C clock and clock stretching per variant: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, 4.1.1 Supported I2C frequencies, p. 9 SE050 ordering and variants: NXP SE050-DATASHEET Rev. 3.8, Table 3 Ordering information, p. 10 SE051 ordering and variants: NXP SE051 Rev. 2.0, Table 2 Ordering information, p. 11 Feature bits of the extended version: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Table 9, p. 26 Limits of FIPS 140-3 mode: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, 3.13.2 FIPS 140-3 mode, p. 45 GetVersion, GetTimestamp, GetFreeMemory, GetRandom: NXP AN12543 Rev. 4.5, Generic management commands, p. 151 SE050 variant identifiers: NXP AN12436 Rev. 2.4, Table 2 Variant identifiers, p. 8 SE051 OEF identifiers per variant: NXP AN12973 Rev. 2.0, Table 4, p. 4 SE052F configuration: applet 7.2.22, AppletConfig 0x26F2, OEF B501: NXP AN14277 Rev. 1.0, SE052F configuration, p. 2 GetFreeMemory reply width: NXP AN13030 Rev. 2.7, GetFreeMemory, p. 641 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Choosing a variant, an applet and an authentication Figure description and sources Read top to bottom; take the first question you answer yes. Certification needs come first: FIPS 140-3 Level 3 is the SE052F; FIPS 140-2 with SCP03 mandatory is the SE050F. Then interfaces: NFC commissioning and Matter (PAKE) is the SE051H, UWB the SE051W. Field update of the applet (SEMS Lite) is the SE051A or C. Otherwise the SE050 by algorithm set: E for AES-GCM and CCM and Curve448 (applet 7.x), C for ECC and RSA, A for ECC only, B for RSA only, D for ECC with MIFARE DESFire. The SE051P runs a customer applet and has no IoT applet, so this driver does not apply. The bottom row is the authentication choice: platform SCP03 whenever the bus can be probed, an ECKey session to bind a host, a UserID session only under a trusted host OS, since it has no secure messaging. The driver reads the real capabilities at Open() and never trusts the part name. Drawn from: inc/se05x_types.hpp ; inc/se05x_caps.hpp ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/variant-decision.py . The driver uses SDA (11) and SCL (10) for the bus and RST_N (14) through the reset port; the SE052 has no ENA pin, so deep power-down is a T=1 S-block (0xDF) and the next I2C access wakes it.
