docs.text: Provisioning and the irreversible operations ¶ Provisioning gives a new device its identity in the factory: open the chip with your platform keys, generate the device keys, record the identity, get the certificates, create the floors, and only then lock what must never change. The locks are irreversible; the driver compiles them only with SE05X_ENABLE_IRREVERSIBLE=1 and applies each only with a plan a person read and a typed confirmation ( Irreversible operations ). The factory provisioning flow Figure description and sources Seven steps in order. Open with the product's platform keys, never the vendor defaults. CheckPlan, then Provision the sign, TLS and agree keys. FactoryRecord: Identify, public keys, attestation. CSR, certificates and trust anchor. CreateCounter makes the anti-rollback floors. Store the network credentials. Then the question Lock? has two answers. Plan, read and confirm leads to Irreversible: RequirePlatformScp, SetLockStatePersistent and DisableObjectCreation. Not yet leads to Ship unlocked, for development only. Drawn from: docs/model/provisioning-flow.graph.yml . /// The factory record: the chip identity and the device public key. template < PortSet P > Error FactoryRecord ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , hrot :: Identity & identity , hrot :: EcPublicKey & public_key ) noexcept { const auto id = hrot . Identify (); if ( ! id . ok ()) { return id . error ; } identity = id . value ; return ProvisionDeviceKey ( hrot , public_key ); // then attest it and send both to your CA } /// Lock the transport for good. Run it from a session with the Transport credential; show the /// plan's effect to a person; the phrase is typed by that person, not by the code that planned it. template < se05x :: PortSet P > se05x :: Error LockForGood ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , const se05x :: irreversible :: Phrase & typed , void ( * show )( const char * effect )) noexcept { using Op = se05x :: irreversible :: SetLockStatePersistent ; se05x :: irreversible :: Operations < P > operations ( device ); const auto plan = operations . PlanSetLockStatePersistent (); // sends nothing if ( ! plan . ok ()) { return plan . error ; // ConditionsNotSatisfied: not a Transport session; WrongState: locked } show ( plan . value . Effect ()); return operations . Apply ( plan . value , se05x :: irreversible :: Confirmation < Op > { typed }). error ; } What it protects against ¶ Threat Answer A device leaving the factory with the vendor's default keys The driver ships no keys; your crypto port holds your key set Bricking a device by a stray call Irreversible operations are compiled out by default and need a plan and a typed confirmation Changing the device later in the field Requiring platform SCP03 and the persistent lock refuse unauthenticated changes (AN12543 3.8, Table 19) Filling slots with objects nobody planned DisableObjectCreation stops new objects after provisioning When it fails ¶ Error Meaning What to do IrreversibleNotConfirmed No plan, a plan for another device, or the wrong phrase Prepare the plan again and confirm it ConditionsNotSatisfied The session role the operation needs is not open Open the session of the role (Transport, FactoryReset, ...) ObjectExists Provisioning ran before Use Find ; do not reprovision Bench step (not verified on hardware): run the full flow on a sacrificial dev kit except the locks, power-cycle and check every Find and CheckFloor ; then plan RequirePlatformScp , confirm, apply, and check a plain command is refused.

docs.text: Store a secret: a Wi-Fi passphrase or a token ¶ Keep the network passphrase, a cloud token or a configuration blob in a binary object of the chip instead of in flash. The object's policy requires secure messaging for every read, write and delete (AN12543 Table 63, pp. 66-67; WriteBinary, AN12543 p. 84; ReadObject, p. 89), and the facade sends it only over a channel that encrypts both ways. Store a secret, load it at every boot Figure description and sources Participants, left to right: Firmware, hrot::Device and SE05x. The steps run from top to bottom. A note over Firmware and SE05x says: provisioning, once. Firmware sends Store(slot 1, passphrase, Secret) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device sends CheckObjectExists, WriteBinary (encrypted, MACed) to SE05x. SE05x returns 9000 (R-MAC checked) to hrot::Device. A note over Firmware and SE05x says: every boot. Firmware sends Load(slot 1, buffer, Secret) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device sends ReadSize, ReadObject (encrypted) to SE05x. SE05x returns the bytes (R-ENC, R-MAC) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device returns SecretBuffer, wiped when it goes out of scope to Firmware. Drawn from: docs/model/store-load-call.seq.yml . /// Keep the Wi-Fi passphrase (or a cloud token) in the chip, written once at provisioning: it /// crosses the bus only encrypted, and the slot refuses a second write (`ObjectExists`). template < PortSet P > Error SaveWifiPassphrase ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan passphrase ) noexcept { return hrot . Store ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 1 > (), passphrase , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ). error ; } /// Read it back at boot into a buffer that wipes itself; nothing else holds a copy. template < PortSet P > Error LoadWifiPassphrase ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , SecretBuffer < 64 >& passphrase ) noexcept { std :: array < uint8_t , 64 > raw {}; const auto n = hrot . Load ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 1 > (), MutableByteSpan { raw }, hrot :: Protection :: Secret ); if ( n . ok ()) { const MutableByteSpan kept = passphrase . Reserve ( n . value ); for ( std :: size_t i = 0U ; i < n . value ; ++ i ) { kept [ i ] = raw [ i ]; } } Zeroize ( MutableByteSpan { raw }); return n . error ; // PolicyDenied without encrypted traffic: open platform SCP03 at Full first } What it protects against ¶ Threat Answer Someone reads the flash of a stolen device The passphrase is not in flash. This holds only if the platform SCP03 keys are not readable from that flash either (a key store a flash copy cannot read): with the keys, the chip opens for anyone A probe on SDA and SCL reads the bytes as they pass The bytes cross the bus encrypted, in a channel at Full A probe replaces the answer Every 9000 answer carries an R-MAC the driver checks in constant time; an error status word comes alone and is not authenticated, so a probe can turn a success into an error, never an error into a success A read of a secret with the wrong protection Load takes the protection you pass. Load(..., Protection::Public) of a secret object over a channel that does not encrypt answers reads it in clear: always pass the protection the object was stored with Firmware overwrites the slot by mistake The slot refuses a second Store with ObjectExists ; Erase first, on purpose A store cut short Store writes a completion marker after the last data chunk; Load refuses an object without it ( FrameError ), so a power loss mid-store never reads back as a value. A store that fails while powered deletes the object, except after SW 0x66A6 ( ThroughputLimited : the chip refuses work, no delete is sent); after a power loss the object stays, without its marker: Erase it and store again (A35) Before the channel is open Until RequirePlatformScp has been applied ( Provisioning ), the chip also answers commands without secure messaging. A probe on the bus can then break your session and send its own plain commands: delete or rewrite Protection::Public data and certificates, and create objects in slots you planned. It cannot read or write Protection::Secret data, whose policy requires secure messaging. Provision in a trusted place, and apply RequirePlatformScp before the device leaves it. Load and Attest read only what Store wrote. An object written another way (by Device or another tool) has no completion marker and is FrameError ; one that happens to end in 0xA5 reads back one byte short. Read such objects with Device::ReadObject . It does not protect against firmware that is itself compromised while it runs: such firmware can call Load like yours does. Keep secrets in the chip and use them there where you can (sign, agree) rather than read them out. When it fails ¶ Error Meaning What to do PolicyDenied (layer Hrot ) The traffic is not encrypted both ways: no platform SCP03 at Full and no AESKey session Open the chip with platform SCP03 at Full ; nothing was sent ObjectExists The slot already holds a value Keep the old value, or Erase() then Store() ObjectNotFound Nothing was stored in the slot Run provisioning BufferTooSmall The stored value is longer than the buffer Use a larger SecretBuffer FrameError The object has no completion marker (a store cut short) or an impossible size Treat the value as unavailable; Erase and store again Bench step (not verified on hardware): cut the power of a dev kit during a 700-byte Store and check that Load returns FrameError . Then, with platform SCP03 open at Full , store a 16-byte passphrase, power-cycle, and load it back; then open without platform SCP03 and check that Load returns PolicyDenied and that a logic analyser sees no ReadObject on the bus.

A note over Firmware and SE05x says: provisioning, once. Firmware sends Store(slot 1, passphrase, Secret) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device sends CheckObjectExists, WriteBinary (encrypted, MACed) to SE05x. SE05x returns 9000 (R-MAC checked) to hrot::Device. A note over Firmware and SE05x says: every boot. Firmware sends Load(slot 1, buffer, Secret) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device sends ReadSize, ReadObject (encrypted) to SE05x. SE05x returns the bytes (R-ENC, R-MAC) to hrot::Device. hrot::Device returns SecretBuffer, wiped when it goes out of scope to Firmware. Drawn from: docs/model/store-load-call.seq.yml . /// Keep the Wi-Fi passphrase (or a cloud token) in the chip, written once at provisioning: it /// crosses the bus only encrypted, and the slot refuses a second write (`ObjectExists`). template < PortSet P > Error SaveWifiPassphrase ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , ByteSpan passphrase ) noexcept { return hrot . Store ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 1 > (), passphrase , hrot :: Protection :: Secret ). error ; } /// Read it back at boot into a buffer that wipes itself; nothing else holds a copy. template < PortSet P > Error LoadWifiPassphrase ( hrot :: Device < P >& hrot , SecretBuffer < 64 >& passphrase ) noexcept { std :: array < uint8_t , 64 > raw {}; const auto n = hrot . Load ( hrot :: DataSlot :: At < 1 > (), MutableByteSpan { raw }, hrot :: Protection :: Secret ); if ( n . ok ()) { const MutableByteSpan kept = passphrase . Reserve ( n . value ); for ( std :: size_t i = 0U ; i < n . value ; ++ i ) { kept [ i ] = raw [ i ]; } } Zeroize ( MutableByteSpan { raw }); return n . error ; // PolicyDenied without encrypted traffic: open platform SCP03 at Full first }
docs.title: Store a secret: a Wi-Fi passphrase or a token

docs.text: Threat Answer Someone reads the flash of a stolen device The passphrase is not in flash. This holds only if the platform SCP03 keys are not readable from that flash either (a key store a flash copy cannot read): with the keys, the chip opens for anyone A probe on SDA and SCL reads the bytes as they pass The bytes cross the bus encrypted, in a channel at Full A probe replaces the answer Every 9000 answer carries an R-MAC the driver checks in constant time; an error status word comes alone and is not authenticated, so a probe can turn a success into an error, never an error into a success A read of a secret with the wrong protection Load takes the protection you pass. Load(..., Protection::Public) of a secret object over a channel that does not encrypt answers reads it in clear: always pass the protection the object was stored with Firmware overwrites the slot by mistake The slot refuses a second Store with ObjectExists ; Erase first, on purpose A store cut short Store writes a completion marker after the last data chunk; Load refuses an object without it ( FrameError ), so a power loss mid-store never reads back as a value. A store that fails while powered deletes the object, except after SW 0x66A6 ( ThroughputLimited : the chip refuses work, no delete is sent); after a power loss the object stays, without its marker: Erase it and store again (A35) Before the channel is open Until RequirePlatformScp has been applied ( Provisioning ), the chip also answers commands without secure messaging. A probe on the bus can then break your session and send its own plain commands: delete or rewrite Protection::Public data and certificates, and create objects in slots you planned. It cannot read or write Protection::Secret data, whose policy requires secure messaging. Provision in a trusted place, and apply RequirePlatformScp before the device leaves it. Load and Attest read only what Store wrote. An object written another way (by Device or another tool) has no completion marker and is FrameError ; one that happens to end in 0xA5 reads back one byte short. Read such objects with Device::ReadObject . It does not protect against firmware that is itself compromised while it runs: such firmware can call Load like yours does. Keep secrets in the chip and use them there where you can (sign, agree) rather than read them out.
docs.title: What it protects against

docs.text: Error Meaning What to do PolicyDenied (layer Hrot ) The traffic is not encrypted both ways: no platform SCP03 at Full and no AESKey session Open the chip with platform SCP03 at Full ; nothing was sent ObjectExists The slot already holds a value Keep the old value, or Erase() then Store() ObjectNotFound Nothing was stored in the slot Run provisioning BufferTooSmall The stored value is longer than the buffer Use a larger SecretBuffer FrameError The object has no completion marker (a store cut short) or an impossible size Treat the value as unavailable; Erase and store again Bench step (not verified on hardware): cut the power of a dev kit during a 700-byte Store and check that Load returns FrameError . Then, with platform SCP03 open at Full , store a 16-byte passphrase, power-cycle, and load it back; then open without platform SCP03 and check that Load returns PolicyDenied and that a logic analyser sees no ReadObject on the bus.

docs.text: Secure channel: SCP03 and why ¶ Without a secure channel every command and answer crosses the I2C bus in clear: a probe on SDA and SCL reads what you store and can rewrite what the chip answers. Platform SCP03 (GlobalPlatform Amendment D, run by the chip's card manager; AN13030 p. 152) encrypts and MACs both directions with session keys derived from static keys only your crypto port holds. An AESKey session does the same per applet session (AN12543 3.6, pp. 33-35). Opening an SCP03 session Figure description and sources Participants, left to right: Device::Open, Crypto port and SE05x card manager. The steps run from top to bottom. Device::Open sends host challenge (Random) to Crypto port. Device::Open sends INITIALIZE UPDATE (host challenge) to SE05x card manager. SE05x card manager returns card challenge, card cryptogram to Device::Open. Device::Open sends derive S-ENC, S-MAC, S-RMAC (CMAC KDF) to Crypto port. A note over Device::Open and SE05x card manager says: Device::Open: check the card cryptogram. Device::Open sends EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE (host cryptogram, level) to SE05x card manager. A note over Device::Open and SE05x card manager says: from here every command: C-MAC (+ C-DEC); every answer: R-MAC (+ R-ENC). Drawn from: docs/model/scp03-open.seq.yml . /// Open the chip with platform SCP03. The keys are handles in your crypto port: never compile key /// bytes into the image, and never use a vendor default key set in a product. template < PortSet P > Error OpenSecure ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , KeyRef platform_enc , KeyRef platform_mac ) noexcept { scp03 :: ChannelParams keys {}; keys . keys . enc = platform_enc ; keys . keys . mac = platform_mac ; if ( const auto given = device . SetPlatformKeys ( keys ); ! given . ok ()) { return given . error ; } return device . Open (). error ; // Config::scp_policy = ScpPolicy::Require when the device was built } /// Open an AESKey session with an authentication object of the chip. `key` is a handle in your /// crypto port; the session ends with EndSession() or Close(). template < PortSet P > Error OpenAesKeySession ( se05x :: Device < P >& device , ObjectId credential , KeyRef key ) noexcept { AesKeySessionParams params {}; params . credential = credential ; params . keys . enc = key ; const auto opened = device . BeginAesKeySession ( params ); if ( opened . error == Error :: NeedsReselect ) { return device . Recover (). error ; // a lost frame under a session: recover, then open it again } return opened . error ; } Choose the level by what you do: keys, counters and verification need authenticated answers ( CMacRMac or Full ), secrets and ECDH need encryption both ways ( Full ). Set Config::scp_policy = ScpPolicy::Require for a root of trust: Auto decides from the chip's unauthenticated ReadState answer, which a probe could change. What it protects against ¶ Threat Answer Reading data on the bus C-DEC and R-ENC encrypt both ways Changing a command or an answer Every command carries a C-MAC and every 9000 answer an R-MAC, checked in constant time. Two answers carry none: an error status word, which comes alone (a probe can turn a success into an error, never the reverse), and the bare 9000 of a command that ends an applet session ( DeleteAll , A22) Replaying an old exchange The MAC chains over the session; the counter never wraps A downgrade to the clear bus Once platform SCP03 was open, the device sends no applet command in the clear until Recover() or Open() has opened it again; those two send the card manager's select and handshake in the clear, as SCP03 requires. With ScpPolicy::Auto , Open() reads the chip's requirement from an unauthenticated answer, so a probe can make it open without SCP03: use Require Before the channel is open Until RequirePlatformScp has been applied, the chip also accepts plain commands, so a probe can send its own whatever your firmware does ( Security model ). Apply it during provisioning. The static keys are the root of this protection: they live in your crypto port as KeyRef handles, never as bytes in the image, and the vendor's default key sets must be replaced before a product leaves the factory. When it fails ¶ Error Meaning What to do AuthFailed Wrong key version or keys Check the key set provisioned for this chip SecureChannelError A MAC or padding check failed The channel is closed; Device::Recover() and open again WrongState The chip requires SCP03 and the policy says Off Give the keys and use Require Bench step (not verified on hardware): open a dev kit with platform SCP03 at Full , trace the bus with a logic analyser and check that no APDU after EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE shows plain data; then flip one bit of an answer in a test harness and check the call fails with SecureChannelError .
